弘治六年進士登科錄

玉音

弘治六年三月十二日，禮部尚書臣耿裕等於奉天門奏為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，太子太傅、戶部尚書兼武英殿大學士徐溥等五十二員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

榮祿大夫、太子太傅、戶部尚書兼武英殿大學士徐溥〔甲戌進士〕。
榮祿大夫、太子太保、禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士丘濬〔甲戌進士〕。
資善大夫、禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士劉健〔庚辰進士〕。
資善大夫、戶部尚書葉淇〔甲戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Register of Metropolitan Graduates for the Sixth Year of Hongzhi (1493)

The Imperial Pronouncement

On the twelfth day of the third month of the sixth year of Hongzhi, your servant Geng Yu, Minister of Rites, and others submitted the following memorial at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations: “The Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm has selected three hundred successful candidates. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we request the appointment of fifty-two officials as readers and other examination functionaries, including Xu Pu, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. The distinctions and ranks conferred upon the metropolitan graduates shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao: the first class shall, according to precedent, comprise three men. The first shall receive the lower sixth rank, and the second and third the upper seventh rank; they shall be granted the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors’ (jinshi jidi). Those in the second class shall receive the lower seventh rank and be granted ‘metropolitan graduate status’ (jinshi chushen). Those in the third class shall receive the upper eighth rank and be granted ‘status equivalent to metropolitan graduate’ (tong jinshi chushen).” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Xu Pu, Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Revenue, concurrently served as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.〕

Qiu Jun, Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites, concurrently served as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.〕

Liu Jian, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Rites, concurrently served as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the gengchen year.〕

Ye Qi was Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Revenue. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month in the sixth year of Hongzhi (1493), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their court robes, standing in their assigned ranks. That day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard arrayed the imperial ceremonial regalia within the vermilion steps and courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and proclaimed the candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow announcement of results, led by drums and music, out beyond Chang’an Left Gate. After it had been posted, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-ranked graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twentieth day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a girdle were bestowed upon the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the rite of offering vegetables (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites submitted a request, and the Ministry of Works was ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education inscribed with the graduates’ names.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the designation “metropolitan graduate with honors” (jinshi jidi).

Mao Cheng 毛澄 was registered in an artisan household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Xianqing and ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bozhen; his grandfather was Bi, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under the applicable regulations; his father was Sheng, and his mother was née Fan. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Hong, Hao, Xie, Jin, and Yuan. His wife was née Xu. He placed forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Mu 徐穆 was registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shunhe and ranked ninth among his brothers. He was twenty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yilun, his grandfather was Shao’an, his father was Tingliang, and his mother was née Zeng. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Shunzai and Shunmei. His wife was née Zhao. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Qinshun 羅欽順 was registered in a military household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Yunsheng and ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-nine years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Cunqian; his grandfather was Duo, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Yongjun, an Academic Corrector at the Nanjing Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Zeng. Both his parents were living. His younger brothers were Qinde and Qinzhong. His wife was née Zeng. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: ninety men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi).

Gu Qing 顧清, of civilian registration in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shilian; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenli, his grandfather Wenxian, his father Qiong, and his mother née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shen, Qin, Shan, Song, and Yan; his wife was née Zhang. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Chaoxuan 謝朝宣, registered with the Xi’an Left Guard in Shaanxi and a native of Linhuai County in the directly administered region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruwei; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather De, his father En, Instructor of the Luoyang County School, and his mother née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chaochong, Chaozheng, Chaoshen, and Chaofu; his wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ying 陳嬰, of civilian registration in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Minhuai; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongli; his grandfather Yanchi held the conferred title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father Mian was Prefect of Fuzhou; and his mother, née Liang, held the conferred title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother Wei was a Messenger; his younger brothers’ names are recorded as 闢𡠾 [?]. His wife was née Hu. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

宋愷〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，儒士，治詩經，字舜臣，行一，年三十三，九月十九日生〕。曾祖仁，祖瓛，父偉〔聽選官〕，母陳氏，繼母周氏。重慶下，弟悌、憤、惇、博、性、懌、恂、忱、桓、樞，娶夏氏。應天府鄉試第二十九名，會試第七十四名。

方璘〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字文玉，行一，年三十六，九月十五日生〕。曾祖師授，祖仲，父寬〔教授〕，母洪氏。慈侍下，弟珎，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第八十九名，會試第二百二十七名。
translation_en:
Zheng Yue 鄭岳, courtesy name Ruhua, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a military-registered student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-six, born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yiqian, his grandfather Tingrang, and his father Zongbo; his mother was née Lin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ruhou, and his wife was née Ye. He placed forty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Huan 劉煥, courtesy name Yaozhang, was registered in a civilian household in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was an added-quota student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, Vice Magistrate of Daning County; his grandfather was Qing; and his father was Ji, Magistrate of Xichuan County. His mother was née Hou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Wei, and his younger brothers were Jiong 煚 and Jiong 炅; his wife was née Zhang. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Kai 宋愷, courtesy name Shunchen, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was a Confucian scholar. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren, his grandfather Huan 瓛, and his father Wei, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Chen, and his stepmother née Zhou. He had living parents and a living grandparent or grandparents. His younger brothers were Ti, Fen, Dun, Bo, Xing, Yi, Xun, Chen, Huan 桓, and Shu; his wife was née Xia. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Lin 方璘, courtesy name Wenyu, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shishou, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Kuan, a prefectural school instructor; his mother was née Hong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Zhen, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed eighty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Yan, courtesy name Shimian, was registered in a civilian household in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yifu; his grandfather, Xiaoyan; his father, Qiong; and his mother, née Xu. His father was still living. His elder brother was Gang, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Xiang, courtesy name Liangbi, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was nineteenth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keheng; his grandfather, Youzhi, had been granted the honorary title of Investigating Censor; his father, Yuan, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Ying, had been granted the title of Lady (ruren). His grandparents and parents were still living. His younger brothers were Dong, Cai, Rong, Pan, and Gai, and his wife was née Pan. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Jiang, courtesy name Yilong, was registered in a civilian household in Xianyou County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengxian; his grandfather, Shaozhong; his father, Ang, was Magistrate of Lu’an Subprefecture; his mother was née Weng, and his stepmother was née Ding. His grandparents and parents were still living. His younger brothers were Chao, Huai, Jian, Mu, Pan, and Ying, and his wife was née Chen. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Huolin, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in an officer household of the Tengxiang Left Guard and was a native of Shanyin County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Gui, was a probationary Company Commander; his grandfather, You, was a substantively appointed Company Commander; his father, Hai, was a Company Commander; and his mother, née Hu, had been granted the title of Lady (anren). His father was still living. His younger brother was Mingfeng, and his wife was née Meng. He placed eighty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Yongzhen, courtesy name Zhongji, was registered with the Chengdu Left Escort Guard in Sichuan and was a native of Liquan County, Shaanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fengxian; his grandfather, Su; his father, Ying; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yonggui, Yongxiang, and Yonghou, and his wife was née Hua. He ranked second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shixian, courtesy name Mengxi, held civilian registration in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kui, County Vice Magistrate of Da County; his grandfather, Sui, a Police Chief; his father, Yu, an Assistant Instructor in the prefectural school of Pengzhou; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shineng, Shijun, and Shiwei, and his wife was née Zeng. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Ke, courtesy name Shengrong, held civilian registration in Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guicun; his grandfather, Yongqi; his father, Shiju; and his mother, née Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shengwen, his younger brother was Shengting, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked twenty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Song, courtesy name Tianting, held civilian registration in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boda; his grandfather, Ang; his father, Bo; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiang, Zhen, Huan, Nan (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions), Yu, and Zhang; his younger brothers were Gui, Huai, Zi, Dong, Liang, and Tong. His wife was née Pan. He ranked ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Tao, courtesy name Liangde, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rizhang; his grandfather, Yiqian, was an Imperial Physician in the Imperial Medical Institute; his father, Zhou, was granted the honorary title of Prefect of Guide Subprefecture; and his mother, née Yang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Jie, was Registrar in the Chief Military Commission of the Right; his younger brothers were Ran and Qiao. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Xia. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Mengyang, courtesy name Tianci, was registered with Qingyang Guard in Shaanxi and was a native of Fugou County, Henan. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was En; his grandfather, Zhong; his father, Zheng, was a Prefectural School Instructor; and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Menghe, a Ceremonial Officer in a princely establishment, and Mengchun; his younger brother was Mengzhang. He married a woman née Zuo. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wen, courtesy name Jingzai, was registered in a civilian household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked thirteenth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Junhai, was a Secretary in the Ministry of War; his grandfather, Minggao, was granted the right to wear official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; his father was Jiben; and his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yongzai, Dazai, and Lizai. He married a woman née Shi and subsequently a woman née Zhong. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Qiong, courtesy name Yufu, was registered in a salt-producing household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongxian; his grandfather, Ren; his father, Xu; and his mother was née Tao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu; his younger brothers were Pu, Yao, Bi, and Shan. He married a woman née Huang. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
錢啓宏，貫直隸松江府華亭縣官籍，國子生，治春秋，字以仁，行一，年三十六，六月初三日生。曾祖惟慶〔贈南京吏部尚書〕，祖溥〔南京吏部尚書贈太子少保謚文通〕，父岡〔義官〕，母朱氏。重慶下，弟啓寅〔監生〕、啓容、啓賓、啓春、啓賢、啓明，娶馬氏。應天府鄉試第一百七名，會試第一百十二名。

馮蘭，貫直隸保定府蠡縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子佩，行一，年三十三，正月十二日生。曾祖吉〔封監察御史贈大理寺卿〕，祖懽〔義官〕，父經〔監生〕，母李氏，繼母張氏。重慶下，弟蓮、蕘、芝、芩、葵，娶鮮氏。順天府鄉試第四十六名，會試第四十二名。

何孟春，貫湖廣郴州民籍，州學生，治易經，字子元，行一，年十九，正月初十日生。曾祖義堅〔州同知〕，祖俊〔按察司僉事〕，父說〔刑部郎中〕，母李氏〔封安人〕。重慶下，弟孟旦，娶歐氏。湖廣鄉試第二名，會試第二十八名。

王承裕，貫陝西西安府三原縣官籍，國子生，治詩經，字天宇，行八，年二十九，三月初五日生。曾祖惟真〔贈太子太保吏部尚書〕，祖智〔贈太子太保吏部尚書〕，父恕〔太子太保吏部尚書〕，嫡母蓋氏〔贈一品夫人〕，繼母張氏〔贈一品夫人〕、文氏，生母張氏。具慶下，兄承祚〔義官〕、承祐〔南京都有經歷〕、承祺、承祿〔義官〕、承祥〔貢士〕、承禮〔義官〕、承禧，弟承禔，娶張氏。陝西鄉試第十一名，會試第二十六名。
translation_en:
Qian Qihong, of an official household registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yiren. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Weiqing was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Personnel at Nanjing; his grandfather Pu was Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wentong. His father Gang was an honorary official, and his mother was née Zhu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Qiyin, a student of the Directorate of Education, Qirong, Qibin, Qichun, Qixian, and Qiming. He married a woman née Ma. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Lan, of a military household registered in Li County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zipei. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Ji was granted the title of Investigating Censor and posthumously granted that of Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. His grandfather Huan was an honorary official, and his father Jing was a student of the Directorate of Education. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Lian, Rao, Zhi, Qin, and Kui. He married a woman née Xian. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Mengchun, of a civilian household registered in Chenzhou, Huguang, was a student of the departmental school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyuan. First in birth order, he was aged nineteen and was born on the tenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Yijian was a Department Vice Magistrate; his grandfather Jun was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his father Shuo was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice. His mother, née Li, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Mengdan. He married a woman née Ou. He placed second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chengyu, of an official household registered in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tianyu. Eighth in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Weizhen and grandfather Zhi were each posthumously granted the titles of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel; his father Shu held those titles. His legal mother, née Gai, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of the First Rank. His stepmothers were a woman née Zhang, likewise posthumously granted the title of Lady of the First Rank, and a woman née Wen; his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengzuo, an honorary official; Chengyou, a Registrar in a Nanjing office whose name is transcribed as 都有 [?]; Chengqi; Chenglu, an honorary official; Chengxiang, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Chengli, an honorary official; and Chengxi. His younger brother was Chengti. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

尚繻，貫河南睢陽衛籍，浙江嘉興縣人，國子生。治《禮記》，字美信，行四，年三十二，三月二十五日生。曾祖雲，祖興，父禧，母高氏，繼母梁氏。具慶下，兄絅〔布政司左參議〕、縉〔臨江知府〕、紳，弟繩、繡。娶張氏。河南鄉試第三十四名，會試第二百十九名。

周季鳳，貫江西南昌府寧縣民籍，國子生。治《春秋》，字公儀，行四，年三十，正月初一日生。曾祖瑾〔金場大使〕，祖銘，父叔襄〔贈兵部員外郎〕，母陳氏〔封太宜人〕。慈侍下，兄季麟〔浙江布政司左參政〕、季驄、季鸞、季鵬、季彪、季邦〔貢士〕。娶方氏，繼娶余氏。江西鄉試第三十九名，會試第十四名。

劉景寅，貫四川叙州府南溪縣民籍，國子生。治《易經》，字生之，行一，年二十八，七月初九日生。曾祖琬，祖恂〔教授贈員外郎〕，父忠〔戶部郎中〕，母鄧氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，弟景宁、景寓。娶郭氏。四川鄉試第四十名，會試第七十三名。

吳一鵬，貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣民籍，國子生。治《易經》，字南夫，行一，年三十四，十一月二十九日生。曾祖敬，祖琮，父行，母司氏，繼母趙氏。具慶下，娶宣氏，繼娶姚氏、薛氏。應天府鄉試第二十三名，會試第二十二名。
translation_en:
Shang Ru, registered with Suiyang Guard in Henan and originally from Jiaxing County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Meixin. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Xing, and his father Xi; his mother was née Gao and his stepmother née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiong, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; Jin, Prefect of Linjiang; and Shen. His younger brothers were Sheng and Xiu. His wife was née Zhang. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Jifeng, of civilian registration in Ning County [?], Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Gongyi. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, Superintendent of a Gold Office; his grandfather was Ming; and his father was Shuxiang, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of War. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title of Grand Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jilin, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang; Jicong; Jiluan; Jipeng; Jibiao; and Jibang, a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Fang and subsequently a woman née Yu. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jingyin, of civilian registration in Nanxi County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shengzhi. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wan; his grandfather was Xun, a Prefectural School Instructor posthumously granted the title of Vice Director; and his father was Zhong, a Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Deng, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jingning and Jingyu. His wife was née Guo. He ranked fortieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yipeng, of civilian registration in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Nanfu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Cong, and his father Xing; his mother was née Si and his stepmother née Zhao. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Xuan and subsequently women née Yao and née Xue. He ranked twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Liangbi 張良弼 was registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Mengzheng, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-two sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiqian, his grandfather Li, and his father Jin, Assistant Prefect of Luanzhou; his mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Liangchen, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Xun 邢珣 was registered in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household, and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ziyong, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-two sui, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Chun, and his father Yu; his mother was née Xia. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jue, Xiang, Ke, and Jie, and his younger brothers Cheng, Lu, and Guang. His wife was née Yang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Jin 白金 was registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household, and was a prefectural-school student. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shizhen, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-seven sui, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouzhong; his grandfather Xiyuan was posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father Ang was Chief Minister of the Office of Imperial Seals at Nanjing. His mother, née Gao, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Zou. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Rong 錢榮 was registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household, and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shien, and he ranked seventh among his brothers. He was thirty-seven sui, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongda, his grandfather Weiyi, and his father Mengpu. His father's former wife was née Hua, and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Quan, Fu, Kai (Instructor in the Medical School), Xiao, and Xi; his younger brothers were Gai, Long, Ling, Ge (Assistant Commander), Zhi, and Shi. His wife was née Zou. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qin Jin 秦金, courtesy name Guosheng, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wuchu, his grandfather Jingxun, and his father Lin; his father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Ming, and his wife was née Niu. He placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yuan 陳元, courtesy name Yuzuo, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Gao, his father Duan, and his mother née Zheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Kai, an official awaiting selection for appointment, Hao, and Ze; his wife was née Qian. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Wensheng 鄒文盛, courtesy name Shiming, was registered in a military household in Gong'an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shimin, his grandfather Huan, his father Lian, and his mother née Yi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenjie and Wenji, his younger brother was Wenxian, and his wife was née Ma. He placed sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Lin 李麟, courtesy name Renzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taiheng, his grandfather Boru, and his father Song; his father's former wife was née Gao, and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, Jie, and Qi; his younger brothers were Tang, a Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and Chang. His wife was née Lai. He placed thirteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xia Congshou, registered in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Rushan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the intercalary seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jingzhao, his grandfather Tinggui, his father Shixun, and his mother née Bao; both parents were living; his younger brother was Congsheng, and his wife was née Zhou; he placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tingyong, registered in Liling County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Liangzuo, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongren, his grandfather Chaogui, his father Ding (Vice Magistrate of Anfu County), and his mother née Wu; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Tingkui and Tinghuan, his younger brothers Tingxiang, Tingrui, and Tingshi, and his wife was née Liu; he placed eleventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Ji, registered in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Jizhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Heng (honorarily invested as Left Case Reviewer), his father Qin, his mother née Liu, and his stepmother née Zhang; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Han, his younger brothers Huai (Medical Instructor), Jie, Qing, Ying, Jing, Cang, Qi, Xiang, Fang, Zhang, Bian, and Cao, and his wife was née Ren; he placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Sheng, registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Qitong, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zongzheng, his grandfather Wenfu, his father Xin, and his mother née Zhou; both parents were living; his elder brother was Ang, and his wife was née Chen; he placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Kuan, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in Yushan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked ninety-third in family order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingren; his grandfather, Xizhe; his father, Yinheng; and his mother, née You. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Liang (Magistrate), Wenzhi, Wenyi, Wende, Wenkuang, and Wenming. He married a woman née Fang. He placed twenty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Pu, courtesy name Liangjin, was registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Huan; his father, Cheng; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rong and Yue. He married a woman née Dong. He placed one hundred twenty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jun, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fourth in family order and was aged twenty-six, born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhifu (Professor); his grandfather, Zhongduan (posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Justice); his father, Feng (Prefect); and his mother, née Zhu (granted the title Lady of Suitability). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhuan (Vice Director in the Ministry of Works) and You; his younger brothers were Wei, Zhong, Dian, Fa, and Yi. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hang Ji, courtesy name Shiqing, was registered in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family order and was aged forty-two, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min; his grandfather, Zheng; his father, Lun; and his mother, née Wang. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Pu; his younger brothers were Yuan, Huai, Lan, Lian, Xun, and Peng. He married a woman née Wang. He placed one hundred thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yi 徐沂, registered in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xizeng, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth month. His elder brothers were Yuan and Yi, and his younger brothers Luo, Huai, Ming, and Tai; he married a woman née Ying. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Hai 郝海, registered in Qizhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Rurong, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Dachu, his grandfather Yuan, his father Wenqing 〔granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations〕, and his mother née Cui; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jiang and Tingyu, and his younger brother Lin; he married a woman née Zheng. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kong Qi 孔琦, registered in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jinghan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather Zhen, his father Jian, and his mother née Xu; his father was deceased and his mother living. An elder brother, Huan, is listed despite his stated rank of first [?]; he married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Qi 范祺, registered in Lishui County, Yingtian Prefecture, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yingzhen, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xiuzhi, his grandfather Yanzhong, his father Jingxin, his legal mother née Zhong, and his birth mother née Zhang; his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yingrong, Yingkuan, and Yinghao, and his younger brother Yingxiang; he married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhao, registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongxian, and his birth order is recorded as “xun two” [?]. He was thirty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiuli, his grandfather Xiaoze, his father Laizheng, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xin and Zai, and his younger brothers Quan, Shen, and Zhi [?]. He married a woman née Hu. He ranked seventy-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jie, registered in Qingjian County, Suide Subprefecture, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shihui, and he was third in birth order. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ren held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Conduct; his grandfather Shangjiong was granted the title of Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his father Yong was Prefect of Changsha; and his mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Luan and Tingzan, and his younger brothers Tingying, Feng, and Tingqi. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked seventeenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chuo, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Benkuan, and he was second in birth order. He was forty years old, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Yuji, his father Gong, and his mother née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yan; Wei, Gong, Gang, and Le are apparently listed as younger brothers [?]. He married a woman née Zheng. He ranked forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan, registered in Wan County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weichen, and he was second in birth order. He was thirty-three years old, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingzu; his grandfather Xi had been granted the right to wear official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; and his father Bin was a Professor, granted the title of Subprefect. His father’s former wife, née Zhao, and his mother, née Gao, were each posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Li. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother Guan was a Prefect. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Zhao, and his father Huan, a student of the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Kan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Feng and Peng, and his wife was née Chen. He ranked seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ce, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. His great-grandfather was Shouyi, his grandfather Youwen, and his father Xun; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Rong, his younger brothers were Fu, Gui, and Biao, and his wife was née Fan. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shixian, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kongzhang. He was third in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Shen, and his father Ze'an, an Instructor at the Military School of the Capital Guards. His mother was née Pan, and his stepmother was née Lin. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother was Shiju, his younger brothers were Shisheng and Shiqian, and his wife was née Zheng. He ranked sixty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Ying, registered in a civilian household in Lin'an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shijie, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen 貞, his grandfather Zhen 真, his father Liu, and his mother née Meng; his parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brother was Mei and his younger brothers Quan and Yue; he married a woman née Qian. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Tingwei, registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yizhong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bocheng, his grandfather Wen, his father Shuqi, his mother née Qian, and his stepmother née Wu; his father alone survived of his parents. His younger brothers were Lin, Tang, Min, Bao, and Shan; he married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed 118th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Dayong, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shixian, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhong, his grandfather Yanming, his father Heng, and his mother née Shen; his mother alone survived of his parents. His elder brothers were Daben, Dazhong, and Daxin, and his younger brothers Daqi and Dayou; he married a woman née Shen. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Ming, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Tianzhang, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Yong〔granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable provisions〕, his father Kui, and his mother née Chen; his parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brother was Zhao; he married a woman née Ma and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lou Su, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongchen, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingye, his grandfather Zhong, his father Da, and his mother née Zhou; both parents were living, his wife was née He, and he placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Yi, registered in Wanzhou, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was originally from Baochang County; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, his courtesy name was Shizhong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhaobao, his grandfather Sheng, his father Mao (Magistrate of Yongjia County), and his mother née Yu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Yong and Duo, his wife was née Wan, and he placed twenty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Yi, registered in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Lianshan, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Wenzhi, his father Li, his father's former wife née Song, and his mother née Chen; his parents and grandparents were deceased, his elder brother was Ming and his younger brother Rui, his wife was née Zhu, and he placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Zixiu, registered in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Renjie, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taizhong, his grandfather Bosheng, his father Zhicheng (Registrar of Taihe County), and his mother née Li; both parents were living, his elder brother was Zimao and his younger brothers Zigao, Ziying, Zichang, and Ziang, his wife was née Zhang, and he placed twenty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zuyou; his grandfather, Jingku; his father, Yong; and his mother, née He. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Geng, Chun, Xiao, and Qiu. His wife was née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Feng, courtesy name Baizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Yingde County, Shaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a native of Nanhai County. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shuibao; his grandfather, Xian; his father, Shan; and his mother, née Xuan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qing, Ao, Dun, and Hui. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Yu, courtesy name Shiwei, was registered in a civilian household in Xia County, Jie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Hongyi; his grandfather, Bin; his father, Chen, was Assistant Prefect of Wuding Subprefecture; and his mother was née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brother Kui was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Li. He placed forty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Heng, courtesy name Zhenfu, was registered with the Fuzhou Central Guard in Fujian and was a native of Min County. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-eight years old, and was born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Bao; his grandfather, Xing; his father, Jun; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tan and Qi. He married women née Wang and née Fu, and subsequently married another woman née Wang. He placed eighty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Jie, courtesy name Zhichu, was registered in a military household in Yongxing County, Chenzhou, Huguang; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rubai; his grandfather, Keqian, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Zhan 䡀, was Prefect of Shaoxing; and his mother, née Chu, was granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tong, and his younger brothers were Quan, a Secretary, Qian, and Nian, a Battalion Commander. His wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Jun, courtesy name Yuchen, was registered in an officer household of the Chenzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongheng; his grandfather was Liang; his father, Yu, was a Company Commander; and his mother was née Liu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Jie, and his wife was née Rui. He placed thirty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shou, courtesy name Deshao, was registered in a civilian household in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture; an Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the twenty-second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongfu; his grandfather, Yuan, was posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his father, Jing, was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi; and his mother, née Hao, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were You, an honorary official, Qi, Xi, and Guan 祼. His wife was née Wang. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Pan, courtesy name Wenyuan, was registered in a military household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked fourteenth among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yawen, was an honorary official; his grandfather was Jiying; his father was Chun; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Han, his younger brother was Pu, and his wife was née Xiong. He placed thirty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yao Mo, courtesy name Yingzhi, was from Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was sixty-first in family order [?] and was born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijing; his grandfather, Ti; his father, Shu; and his mother, née Hu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Ming, courtesy name Yuding, was from Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, registered in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in family order, aged thirty [?], and was born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianzu; his grandfather, Jingcan; his father, Qi; his mother, née Cai; and his stepmother, née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lin, Heng (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), Mao, and Quan. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shunfu, courtesy name Congren, was from Xindu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in family order, aged forty-two [?], and was born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Qing (a District Magistrate); his father, Ang; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yufu and Tangfu. He married a woman née Han. He placed sixty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Fan, courtesy name Xuanzhi, was from Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a military household. A department school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in family order, aged thirty [?], and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziyu; his grandfather, Yan; his father, Da (Vice Magistrate of Yin County); his mother, née Zhang; and his birth mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Bi 劉弼, of Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhizhi, and he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Quan and grandfather Lang were both posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; his father Chan was a retired Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and his mother, née Li, held the title Shuren. Both parents were living. His elder brother Fu was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Tian. He placed thirty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yu 周玉, of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Chaozhen, and he was second in birth order, aged forty-three, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather Xian was posthumously appointed Administrator, and his father Chang was an Administrator. His mother, née Xie, held the title Yiren. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zan; his younger brothers were Wen, Ke, a Professor, and Qiu. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Cheng 陸偁, of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a military household and was a prefectural government student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Junmei, and he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yingxiang, his grandfather Qi, his father Huan, and his mother a woman née Qian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xie, Yi 儀, Biao, and Yi 佾. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twentieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xun 王恂, of Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shicheng, and he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Dehua was a prefectural Registrar; his grandfather was Zhongji, and his father Sheng was Commissioner of a Transport Office. His mother was a woman née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yu, Kai, and Ti, and his younger brother was Yi. He married a woman née Tang and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yi 盧儀, registered in Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhengfu; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongcheng, his grandfather Lun, and his father Rugong, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi, Xian, Yin, Guan, and Yong, and his younger brothers Feng, Jun, Ren, and Ji. His wife was née Wei. He placed fourteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chong 王翀, registered in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingfeng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yingzhen, his grandfather Yi, and his father Dashao; his mother was née Gou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yong and Qian, and his wife was née Feng. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Ze 黃澤, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruoyu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the intercalary ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhong, his grandfather Zuyang, and his father Zicun. His father's former wife was née Liang, and his mother was née He. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Wen, Hong, and Qian. His wife was née Wu; he subsequently married a woman née Mo. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chu Qi 褚圻, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Hongwang; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sigong, his grandfather Gongyi, and his father Yu, an Erudite in the Nanjing Directorate of Education. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yin was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brother was Tan. His wife was née Xie. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Chunfu; he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongliang, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Zhicheng, Assistant Instructor at the Shouchang County Confucian School; his mother was née Zou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jun and Liu, and his younger brother was Han. His wife was née Long. He ranked ninety-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Lan, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuanxu; he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boteng, his grandfather Limin, and his father Yuying; his mother was née Zheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Wu. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xian, registered in Anlu Subprefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shimin; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eleventh day of the intercalary eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuzu, his grandfather Gui, granted the title of Subprefect of Chuzhou, and his father Zheng, Prefect of Datong; his mother was née Zhu, granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Qi, and his younger brothers were Yin, Bin, and Ning. His wife was née Song. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lin, registered in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bangrui; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fuju; his grandfather, Rong; and his father, Zhi, Department Magistrate of Jingzhou. His mother was née Shang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi, and his younger brother was Gui. His wife was née Yan. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chun, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiwen; he ranked twenty-sixth in the family order and was aged thirty, born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zuchang, Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather, Qian; and his father, Guan. His mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ji; his younger brothers were Ji and Qi. His wife was née Li. He placed sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Lian, registered in Anding County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weiqing; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Keyun; and his father, Zheng. His mother was née Cheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhongli and Zhongyi. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Erhe 楊二和 was registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Fanfu. He ranked eighteenth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-one, and was born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongwen; his grandfather, Jingshan, was granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Jun, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang. His father’s former wife, née Rao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren); his mother, née Wu, was granted the same title. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His elder brother was Yihe, and his wife was née Xu. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jian 陳諫 was registered in a military household in Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rubi. He ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather was Zongtai; his father, Yan, was a Study Companion; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xun, his younger brothers were Hui, Ne, and Rang, and his wife was née Li. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shi 李實 was registered in a military household in Ba County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruoxu. He ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-five, and was born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shi’an; his grandfather, Hai, was Magistrate of Luoci County; his father, Jing, had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhen, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Mao 于瑁 was registered in a military household in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chaorui. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xiaoxian; his grandfather was Xing; his father, Kai, held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness (yiguan); and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xuan and Tang, and his wife was née Meng. He placed seventieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

杜旻〔貫錦衣衛，官籍，直隸山陽縣人，儒士，治詩經，字德仁，行六，年二十三，十二月初二日生〕。曾祖保〔千戶〕，祖方〔贈千戶〕，父春〔副千戶〕，前母陳氏、楊氏，母江氏。具慶下，兄亨、義、昱、昇、禮，弟杲，娶陳氏。順天府鄉試第十一名，會試第一百十五名。

余濂〔貫江西南康府都昌縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字宗周，行二，年三十，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖仲慶，祖伯誠，父嵩〔推官〕，母翁氏，繼母白氏。慈侍下，兄瀾，娶髙氏。江西鄉試第二十四名，會試第八十三名。
translation_en:
Wang Yingkui, courtesy name Wenrui, was registered in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hu; his grandfather, Zhang; and his father, Jue, assistant prefect of Mangbu Prefecture. His mother was née Mu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yingrong and Yinghua, and his wife was née Li. He placed first in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yuan, courtesy name Deyuan, was registered in Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gang, posthumously appointed a prefectural vice prefect; his grandfather, Shi, a prefect; and his father, Xian, a county magistrate. His mother was née Ding, and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ren, Kuan, and Guan. His wife was née Lü; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed 113th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Min, courtesy name Deren, was registered in an official household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Shanyang County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked sixth among his brothers, was aged twenty-three, and was born on the second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Bao, a battalion commander; his grandfather, Fang, posthumously appointed a battalion commander; and his father, Chun, a vice battalion commander. His father's former wives were née Chen and née Yang, and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Heng, Yi, Yu, Sheng, and Li; his younger brother was Gao. His wife was née Chen. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Lian, courtesy name Zongzhou, was registered in Duchang County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhongqing; his grandfather, Bocheng; and his father, Song, a prefectural judge. His mother was née Weng, and his stepmother was née Bai. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Lan, and his wife was née Gao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.
