夏璲〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字廷贊，行五，年四十，六月二十日生。〕曾祖雷甫〔元萬戶〕，祖時用，父以明〔義官〕，嫡母張氏，繼母景氏，生母陳氏。慈侍下，兄琮、瓛〔府同知〕、玘、璧，弟璜，娶賈氏。應天府鄉試第八十八名，會試第一百十七名。

趙繼爵〔貫陝西西安府同州，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字世忠，行三，年二十九，正月十四日生。〕曾祖仁義，祖玉，父琰〔鹽課司大使〕，母張氏。重慶下，兄繼祖、繼宗，弟繼祿，娶劉氏。陝西鄉試第六十四名，會試第一百八十三名。

姜閔〔貫山東登州府黃縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字道淵，行二，年三十三，正月二十日生。〕曾祖業，祖浩，父文〔教授〕，母陳氏。具慶下，兄瓚，弟闢，娶王氏。山東鄉試第十五名，會試第六十三名。

彭縉〔貫湖廣襄陽府襄陽縣，匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字文卿，行一，年三十五，十二月十五日生。〕曾祖仁，祖英〔贈大理寺評事〕，父銓〔大理寺右寺正〕，母李氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，弟綱、紀、紳、經、綸、編、緒，娶艾氏。湖廣鄉試第二十七名，會試第二百三十六名。
translation_en:
Xia Sui, registered in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingzan. Fifth in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Leifu, a myriad commander under the Yuan; his grandfather was Shiyong; and his father was Yiming, an honorary official. His father's principal wife was née Zhang, his stepmother née Jing, and his birth mother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Cong, Huan (a prefectural vice prefect), Qi, and Bi; his younger brother was Huang. He married a woman née Jia. He placed eighty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jijue, registered in Tongzhou Subprefecture, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shizhong. Third in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the fourteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Renyi; his grandfather was Yu; and his father was Yan, commissioner of a Salt Tax Office. His mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jizu and Jizong, and his younger brother was Jilu. He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Min, registered in Huang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Daoyuan. Second in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the twentieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ye; his grandfather was Hao; and his father was Wen, a professor. His mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zan, and his younger brother was Pi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Jin, registered in Xiangyang County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenqing. First in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ren; his grandfather was Ying, posthumously appointed case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; and his father was Quan, right rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review. His mother, née Li, had been granted the title Lady (Ruren). His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Gang, Ji, Shen, Jing, Lun, Bian, and Xu. He married a woman née Ai. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡燿〔貫直隸太平府蕪湖縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字仲光，行三，年四十二，十二月初八日生〕。曾祖泰，祖潛，父杲，母侯氏，繼母范氏。永感下，兄煜、烜，弟炳、薰、熹、照、爚，娶洪氏。應天府鄉試第十四名，會試第一百一名。

常賜〔貫山西澤州沁水縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字承恩，行四，年二十六，三月二十三日生〕。曾祖謙，祖瑜〔贈大理寺評事〕，父昌雲，母賈氏。永感下，兄贇、賢、質，弟貢、貫、勛，娶張氏。山西鄉試第一名，會試第二百四十九名。
translation_en:
Xu Yi, registered in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongxing. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guoxiang, his grandfather Yanli, and his father Tingyu; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Fu, and his wife was née Zhou. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Zhi, registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Hefei County in the Metropolitan Region, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenming. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Fu was posthumously appointed Vice Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his grandfather Shun held that office. His father Sheng was a retired Battalion Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His legal mother, née Ji, held the title Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother Long was a Full Battalion Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. He married a woman née Zhou, and subsequently women née Yan and née Zhu. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yao, registered in Wuhu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongguang. He was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Qian, and his father Gao; his mother was née Hou and his stepmother née Fan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yu and Xuan; his younger brothers were Bing, Xun, Xi, Zhao, and Yue. His wife was née Hong. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Ci, registered in Qinshui County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Cheng'en. He was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather Yu was posthumously appointed Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. His father was Changyun and his mother née Jia. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yun, Xian, and Zhi; his younger brothers were Gong, Guan, and Xun. His wife was née Zhang. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

盧瀚〔貫直隸揚州府江都縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字文淵，行一，年二十六，六月二十八日生〕。曾祖勝，祖錦〔遞運所大使〕，父垕，母劉氏，繼母俞氏。慈侍下，弟潮、淞，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第七十七名，會試第六十七名。
translation_en:
Dong Sigong, registered in Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jinxian; he was fourth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Lianghui, a department magistrate under the Yuan; his grandfather was Ji; and his father was Sheng, a county vice magistrate posthumously granted the title of bureau director. His father’s former wife, née Guo, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother, also née Guo, was granted the title Senior Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Fengxian, Sizhong, surveillance vice commissioner in Sichuan, and Sicheng, vice director of a bureau in the Ministry of Personnel. He married a woman née Xue and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kuang Fan, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingrui; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Keduan, his grandfather Fu, and his father Guanzheng, a county vice magistrate; his mother was née Yin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun and Yu, and his younger brothers Heng, Ju, and Cong. He married a woman née Xu. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Qing, registered in Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruyang; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Andao, his grandfather Yi, and his father Xian. His father’s former wife was née Ba, his mother née Chen, and his stepmother née Cao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Cheng, and his younger brothers Hao, Lian, Yuan, and Han. He married a woman née Yan and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Han, registered in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenyuan; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Jin, commissioner of a transport office; and his father was Hou. His mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Yu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Chao and Song. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventy-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zhen 王縝, courtesy name Wenzhe, was registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fourteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chunli, his grandfather Chen, and his father Ke, Prefect of Baoqing; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zujing and Zuwei. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yao 徐瑶, courtesy name Cuiqing, was registered in Changshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked thirty-second in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanwen, his grandfather Yongxi, posthumously awarded the title of Investigating Censor, and his father Tong’ai, an Investigating Censor. His mother, née Cheng, held the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen and Xiu, and his younger brothers Bi and Chong. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Duan 鄭端, courtesy name Sizhi, was registered with the Linqing Guard in Shandong and was a native of Yancheng County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Linqing Subprefectural School specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty years old, born on the thirtieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather You, and his father Jun; his mother was née Tang and his stepmother née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kai, Cong, and Ming. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed thirty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Xin 何歆, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in Boluo County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhijie, his grandfather Zhengyuan, and his father Cang. His father’s former wife was née Wang, his mother née Chen, and his stepmother née Yu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Wenjin, and his younger brothers Wenlong, Wenguang, Wensheng, and Wenshang. He married a woman née Guo. He placed fifty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Shining 胡世寧, courtesy name Yongqing, was registered in a civilian household in Changhua County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Renhe County; a student of the Changhua County school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Song, his father Rong, and his mother Lady Feng; both parents were living. His elder brother was Shikang, and his younger brothers were Shixian and Shiliang; he married Lady Li. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Lan 徐瀾, courtesy name Wenyuan, was registered in a military household in Wuqing County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Sixiao, Magistrate of Dong'e County, his father Jing, Magistrate of Jishan County, and his mother Lady Liu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Pu and Chun, and his younger brothers were Yan, Yi, Zhu, Jie, and Zhi; he married Lady Su. He placed ninetieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Wenyuan 辛文淵, courtesy name Daoshen, was registered in a military household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Shouzhong, his father Xian, and his mother Lady Li; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Wenyu, an Honorary Official (yiguan), and Wenqing, and his younger brothers were Wenjie and Wenze; he married Lady Wu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xiwen 鄭錫文, courtesy name Yufan, was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shu, his grandfather Xuan, his father Tan, his mother Lady Chen, and his successive stepmothers Ladies Lin and Huang; his father was deceased and a mother living. His younger brother was Xiwu; he married Lady Gao. He placed forty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Peng, registered in an artisan household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was Instructor at the Rongcheng County School in the directly administered metropolitan region; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Kongteng, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhining, his grandfather Jinghe, and his father Shanyuan; his mother was née Lin, and his stepmothers were née Gao and née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Qiaoling, Changling, and Tangling, and his younger brother was Deling; he married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jing, registered in a military household in Jiang County, Jiang Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Yaofu, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Zheng (a prefectural Investigator), and his father Wei; his mother was née Guo. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Cong, Yu, and Zhen, and his younger brother was Lian (a tribute scholar, gongshi); he married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Da, registered in an artisan household in Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Shangda, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged forty, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Gui, and his father Peng (a student of the Directorate of Education); his mother was née Fan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kui and Lian, and his younger brothers were Di, Yuan, and Rui; he married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Ren. He placed twenty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yu, registered with the Chengdu Left Escort Guard in Sichuan and a native of Renshou County, was a county school student; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Tingbi, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingxian (a Registrar), his grandfather Mao (honorarily granted the title of Secretary), and his father Yuan (Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guizhou); his mother was née Li (granted the title Lady of Peace). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Pu, and his younger brothers were Zan, Chen, and Fan; he married a woman née Fang. He placed thirty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He was seventh in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yizhong; his grandfather, Caishang; his father, Jing, Assistant Instructor at the Wuyuan County School; and his mother, née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ji, Sheng, Gang, Shou, Lü, and Xuan; his younger brothers were Shen, Hao, and Jin. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ruan Bin 阮賓, courtesy name Junpin, was registered with the Front Imperial Guard and was a native of Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi. A student of the Shuntian Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Da; and his mother, née Li 黎. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Li 李. He ranked ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yun 李允, courtesy name Xinzhi, was a native of Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, registered in an artisan household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renhai; his grandfather, Ming, Magistrate of Xiajin County; his father, Jikang; and his mother, née Meng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Li 曆. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Lü. He ranked seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ao 李鏊, courtesy name Shiji, was registered in a civilian household in Tongwei County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingwen, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; his grandfather was Hong; his father, Liangyu, a student of the National University; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kai and Qi. He married a woman née Guo. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Yong 雷顒, registered in Luzhou Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingzhi; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongde, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Keliang; his father's former wife was née Qin, and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xian, Tong, and Kuan. He married a woman née Wen and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Gao 武皐, registered in Hezhou Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shunbi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanxin, his grandfather Bin, his father Guang, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiu, and his younger brothers were Lin and Zhi. He married a woman née Xu 許. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pang Cong 龐璁 was registered in an officer household of the Wugong Left Guard and was a native of En County, Shandong. He was a supplementary student of the Shuntian prefectural school and specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Runfu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Youzhi, grandfather Gui, and father Fu were all company commanders. His mother, née Jin, had been granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Li, and his younger brothers were Zan and Yu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 103rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Zhongren; he ranked first in birth order and was forty-six years old, born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Yu, his father Ying, and his mother née Chen. His father alone was still living. His younger brothers were Gongze and Gongpu. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently another woman née Lin. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Shi was registered in a guardsman's household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Jizhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yinzheng; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Bin, his father Guang, and his mother née Yi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cheng and his younger brother Jingchang. He married a woman née Tang. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Zhongxian, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Liangfu; he ranked fourth in birth order and was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ziming; his grandfather Wenbin and father Shikuan both held the title of honorary official; his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhongshun, Zhongxin, and Zhongxian, and his younger brothers were Zhongfeng, Zhonglun, Zhongbi, Zhongbing, and Zhongzhen. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Xiyan, registered in a military household in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jingxian; he ranked sixtieth in birth order and was twenty-six years old, born on the third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qiyuan, his grandfather Ying, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations, his father Shunfu, and his mother née Qiu. His grandfather and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiyu, Xi, and Ti, and his younger brothers were Xihu, Yin, and Zhen. He married a woman née Shu and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Xu. He placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Xuan, courtesy name Shenjian, was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xueshao; his grandfather, Kehe; his father, Jishi; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shenyu, Shenlü, Shendu, Shende, and Shenzhong. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He ranked ninety-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Yong, courtesy name Mingyuan, was registered with Gongchang Guard in Shaanxi and was a native of Huating County in the directly administered region. An Instructor at the Xinxiang County Confucian School specializing in the Record of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Wenzhen, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; his father, Pu; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jin and Yue. He married a woman née Xia. He ranked fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Xi, courtesy name Shouzheng, was registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Instructor at the Wujin County Confucian School in the directly administered region specializing in the Book of Odes, he was thirty-eighth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Boyuan, posthumously granted the title of Administration Vice Commissioner; his grandfather, Zhongkuan; his father, Jian, an Instructor; and his mother, née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Hong, Fen, Shouxin, Shouxing, and Jin. He married a woman née Shen. He ranked fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shi, courtesy name Shizhong, was registered with Guilin Central Guard in Guangxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chengcun; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Ming; and his mother, née Jin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Hui. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

郭瑀〔貫和陽衛官籍，直隸灤州人，京衛武學生，治詩經，字佩之，行二，年四十，十月二十七日生〕。曾祖道童〔贈昭勇將軍指揮使〕，祖玉〔指揮使〕，父亨〔指揮使〕，母鄭氏〔封淑人〕，繼母王氏。永感下，兄瑛〔本衛指揮使〕，娶党氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十五名，會試第七十五名。
translation_en:
Yu Chun 蔚春 was registered in a medical household in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Jingyuan and was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guan, his grandfather Zhen, his father Qing, and his mother née Yang. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Gao, Shi, Xiao, Ang, and Zhi; his wife was née Fan. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yan 劉演 was registered in a civilian household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Wenfu and was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jingyi and grandfather Mengrong were each posthumously appointed Investigating Censor. His father was Jue, his mother née Shen, and his stepmother née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lan 瀾, Pang, Se, Bo, Bian, Luan, Chao, Qu, Guan, and Gang; his wife was née Ye. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lan 劉蘭 was registered in a military household in Qingjian County, Suide Subprefecture, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Tingfu and was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jie was Assistant Instructor in that county; his grandfather Wendao was posthumously appointed Prefect; his father Mai was a Registry Manager in Shunqing Prefecture; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hui and his younger brother Ai; his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Yu 郭瑀 was registered in an officer household of Heyang Guard and was a native of Luanzhou in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student at the military school of the capital guards specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Peizhi and was second in birth order, aged forty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Daotong was posthumously granted the title General of Illustrious Courage and the office of Guard Commander. His grandfather Yu 玉 and father Heng were Guard Commanders. His mother, née Zheng, was granted the title Lady of Gentleness; his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Ying was Commander of the same guard; his wife was née Dang. He placed 135th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Zaide, registered in Xinzheng County, Jun Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Gongzhu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Jing, and his father Min, a prefectural vice prefect; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zaixiao, Zailian, Zaiyi, and Zairen, and his wife was née Feng. He ranked thirtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Zan, registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Boheng; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Gui, his father Wenju, and his mother née Wu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Cong, his younger brothers Zhang, Lian, and Xuan, and his wife was née Li. He ranked fiftieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Kai, registered in Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Liangzuo; he was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kecheng, his grandfather Shixian, and his father Gang, magistrate of Huoqiu County; his father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guang, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions, and Chong; his wife was née Yang. He ranked seventieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Xun, registered in Jun Subprefecture, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongrang; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingyun, his grandfather Youcai, posthumously granted the title of subprefectural vice magistrate, and his father Zhong, magistrate of Dongping Subprefecture; his mother, née Jin, had been granted the title of Lady of Repose. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gong, Jing, who had been granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations, and Qian; his younger brother was Ke. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Lu. He ranked seventy-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ren Liangbi was registered in a civilian household in Pingyao County, Fenzhou, Shanxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingzan. Second in birth order, he was thirty-two years old and was born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xiao; his grandfather, Yi, was Magistrate of Qianshan County; and his father was Hui. His father's former wife was née Zhang, his mother was née Fan, and his stepmother was née Ji. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother, Liangcai, was Magistrate of Jiangyin County; his younger brothers were Liangzuo, Liangqing, Liangkui, Liangshi, Liangxi, Lianghan, and Liangxiang. He married a woman née Lei. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Ju was registered in an officer household of the Yunnan Rear Guard and was a native of Dingyuan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daqi. Fourth in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Cheng, was an Assistant Commander; his grandfather, Ji, was a Commander; and his father, Qi, was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His mother, née Cao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Virtue. His parents were both deceased. His elder brothers were Zheng, Jing, who was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, and Min. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventeenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shou was registered in a military household in Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chaoyi. Second in birth order, he was twenty-five years old and was born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sicheng; his grandfather was Ying; and his father, Xin, was granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites. His mother, née Shi, was granted the title of Lady. Both his parents were living. His elder brother, Lun, was a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; his younger brothers were Ji, Xu, and Shen. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qing was registered in a military household in Lingbao County, Shanzhou, Henan Prefecture, Henan, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongshan. Second in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Fu; and his father, Shi, was a student of the Directorate of Education. His mother was née Shao, and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both his parents were living. His elder brother was Xing; his younger brothers were Kun, Chen, Kai, Dun, and Ke. He married a woman née Meng. He placed fifty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Ju, courtesy name D聘 (Daping), was registered in an officer household of Zhenwu Guard in Shanxi and was a native of Hequ County, Taiyuan Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the thirtieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Rong, and his father Jingchang; his father’s former wife was née Shen, and his mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Tang, Ji, Jian, and Dian. He married a woman née Shi. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Yingqi, courtesy name Sizheng, was registered in a military household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bi, his grandfather Xin, his father Guan, and his mother née Hu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Yingwang. He was betrothed to a woman née Shen. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian You, courtesy name Tingxiang, was registered in an officer household of the Imperial Bodyguard Front Guard and was a native of Ganyu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An added-quota student at the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged twenty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zicai, posthumously granted the title of Commander; his grandfather Gui was Vice Regional Military Commissioner, serving as Left Assistant Regional Commander; and his father Tong was a Commander. His father’s former wives were née Men, granted the title of Lady of Virtue, and née Ding; his mother was née Wang, also granted the title of Lady of Virtue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ying, a Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; Cong; Fu; Zuo, a Commander; and Fang. His younger brothers were Bi and Yuan. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhang. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Xun, courtesy name Keshan, was registered in a military household in Xugou County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Wei, his father Fang, an official in a River Tax Office, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi and Ji. He married a woman née Dong. He placed fifty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cao Qiong, registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingyu; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jueguang, his grandfather Xian, and his father Tianshou; his father's principal wife and his birth mother were both née Zhu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ming, Xiang, and Feng, and his wife was née Zhan. He placed sixtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Qian, registered in a civilian household in Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianyi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Bing (Police Chief), and his father Cong (Magistrate of Linyi County); his mother was née Xie. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Xiang, Shi, and Yi, and his wife was née Wu. He placed seventieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhao, registered in a civilian household in Caozhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jizong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, his grandfather Shu, and his father Heng (Commissioner of a Salt Tax Office); his father's former wife was née Chang, and his mother was née Li. Both his parents were deceased. His younger brother was Wei; he married a woman née Cheng and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed forty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ru, registered in a civilian household in Yuhang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiyong; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-two years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingming, his grandfather Huan, and his father Xian; his mother was née Fang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Ren, his younger brothers were Wu and Chuan, and his wife was née Shen. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Shun, of Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zihua. Eighth in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, honored as a righteous commoner; his grandfather was Hui; his father was Zhuo; and his mother was née Sima. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Yuan, Ba, Luo, and Hong; his younger brothers were Li, Gao, Yuqing, and Kuilong [the division of the last names is uncertain]. He married a woman née Shen. He placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yi, of Yongshou County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was registered in a yin-yang specialist household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zongde. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, an Instructor in Yin-yang Studies; his grandfather was Ming; and his father was Zhen, also an Instructor in Yin-yang Studies. His father’s former wife was née Yao, his mother was née Cao, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing, Shou, and Wei, the last a student of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Kang and subsequently a woman née Yuwen. He placed thirty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xuan, of Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shida. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongyu; his grandfather was Jingdun; his father was Bohao, an honorary official; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hong. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Rang, of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Benhou. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenpi [?]; his grandfather was Qian; his father was E; and his mother was née Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yu, Yuan, and He. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Qing, courtesy name Tiande, was registered in a military household in Pingshan County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five sui, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renmei; his grandfather, Rang; his father, Zhang, Assistant Office Director in the Court of State Ceremonial; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Xu was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi). He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ting, courtesy name Weiji, was registered in a military household in Qian'an County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Xi; his father, Lun; his mother, née Shen; and his stepmother, née Huo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chen and Zhang. He married a woman née Lu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ke Gongbei, courtesy name Dounan, was registered in an officer household of the Chengdu Rear Guard in Sichuan and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanfang; his grandfather, Bengeng; his father, Jun; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gongchen and Gongzong, and his younger brothers were Gonghuan and Gongxian. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Zhang, courtesy name Yongyu, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked ninth among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Wei, Magistrate of Haifeng County; his father, Huai; and his mother, née Chen. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fiftieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Xiong, registered in a military household in Yongqing County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shijie; he ranked second in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather Wenzhi, his father Hai, and his mother née Gao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xuan and his younger brother Qi. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Yong. He placed forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hong, registered with Guangyang Guard in Nanjing and a native of Liuhe County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shuyi; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiuweng, his grandfather Shezong, his father Qing, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tai, and he married a woman née Shi. He placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Xigu, registered in a military household in Xinning County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shangyou; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Zhen, his father Kan (a National University student), and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xishang; his younger brothers were Xixian, Xiyi, and Xida. He married a woman née Fu. He placed tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Maonan, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chaoliang; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiqin, his grandfather Boming, and his father Shiyi (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions). His mother was née Chen, and his stepmothers were née Wu and née Guo. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Maoxun, Jingling (a Post Station Master), Maozhang, and Maojiang (a National University student); his younger brother was Maoqi. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Feng Jing, a National University student registered in a military household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiji; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Rang, vice magistrate of Dantu County; his grandfather was Xuan, granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; his father was Zan, and his mother was née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ji and Shou. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengxun, a Confucian scholar registered in a postal-relay household in Jiayu County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Liqing; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged twenty-three, born on the eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a police chief posthumously granted the title of right vice censor-in-chief; his grandfather was Shan, a director of schools posthumously granted the same title; his father was Tian, right vice censor-in-chief; and his mother was née Bi, granted the title of Lady of Virtue. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Chengye, Chengfang (case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review), Chengji (tribute student), Cheng'en (a student admitted by virtue of his father's official status), and Chengyan; his younger brothers were Chengxin and Chengjie. He married a woman née Gong. He placed eleventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tingce, registered in a commoner household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an added student of the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yiyang; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Fuqian, his grandfather Hunyang, and his father Xunyong; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Kuang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Tingchi, Tingjian, and Tingchou. He married a woman née Kuang. He placed eighty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ji, a National University student registered in a salt-producing household in Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shunzai; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yanchang, prefect of Daming; his grandfather was Yi, and his father Che. His father's former wife was née Wen, and his mother was née Duan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zan, Chen (vice magistrate of Luotian County), Yu (professor in the household of the Prince of Longyang [?]), Xuan 瑄, and Xuan 璇; his younger brothers were Shan, Zhen, Qiang, Ke, and Pei. He married a woman née Mu 母. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉武臣〔貫四川叙州府宜賓縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字希召，行四，年三十九，十月二十九日生〕。曾祖仕華，祖澣〔監察御史〕，父山〔陰陽正術〕，母李氏。嚴侍下，兄堯臣、舜臣、周臣，弟唐臣、藎臣〔陰陽正術〕、近臣，娶周氏。四川鄉試第十一名，會試第三十名。

王子成〔貫湖廣武昌府咸寧縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字公大，行一，年三十四，十月三十日生〕。曾祖本〔無為州吏目〕，祖禎，父紹〔義官〕，母戴氏。具慶下，弟子俊、子英、子卿，娶韓氏。湖廣鄉試第十九名，會試第二百二名。

郭浹〔貫湖廣武昌府興國州軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字從仁，行四，年二十八，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖志輔，祖銓〔倉副使〕，父琮〔進賢縣丞〕，母田氏。具慶下，兄濟、洧、泗，弟泮，娶余氏。湖廣鄉試第五十名，會試第一百十九名。

孫徽〔貫湖廣襄陽護衛籍，直隸虹縣人，國子生，治詩經，字德夫，行二，年三十四，二月十八日生〕。曾祖旺，祖耕，父義，母高氏，繼母李氏。重慶下，兄通，弟裕、繡、嶽、嵩，娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百九十八名。
translation_en:
Liu Wuchen, registered in a military household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xizhao; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shihua; his grandfather, Han, was an Investigating Censor; his father, Shan, was Director of the School of Yin-yang Studies; and his mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Yaochen, Shunchen, and Zhouchen; his younger brothers were Tangchen, Jinchen, who was Director of the School of Yin-yang Studies, and Jinchen (近臣). His wife was née Zhou. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zicheng, registered in a military household in Xianning County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Gongda; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the thirtieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Ben, was a Clerk of Wuwei Subprefecture; his grandfather was Zhen; his father, Shao, held the honorary title of Righteous Official; and his mother was née Dai. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zijun, Ziying, and Ziqing. His wife was née Han. He placed nineteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Jia, registered in a military household in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Congren; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhifu; his grandfather, Quan, was a Vice Commissioner of a Granary; his father, Cong, was Assistant Magistrate of Jinxian County; and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji, Wei, and Si; his younger brother was Pan. His wife was née Yu. He placed fiftieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Hui, registered with the Xiangyang Princely Escort Guard in Huguang and originally from Hong County in Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather was Geng; his father was Yi; his mother was née Gao; and his stepmother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Tong; his younger brothers were Yu, Xiu, Yue, and Song. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉賢〔貫四川潼川州射洪縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字世資，行二，年三十三，十月初十日生〕。曾祖景鴻，祖長器，父持漢，母高氏。具慶下，兄芳，弟傑，娶楊氏。四川鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百五十七名。

林坴〔貫福建福州府閩縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字世集，行六，年三十九，十月初五日生〕。曾祖必芳，祖果，父汝白，母陳氏。永感下，兄墪、壎〔湖廣參政〕、墠、璧〔禮部郎中〕，弟𡐤、坒〔貢士〕，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第七十八名，會試第二百二十四名。

王昊〔貫湖廣衡州府衡陽縣，馬船夫籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝欽，行四，年三十八，七月二十四日生〕。曾祖思誠，祖添勝，父貴，母李氏。慈侍下，兄洪、湖、潮，弟潤、澗，娶許氏。湖廣鄉試第六十三名，會試第二百八名。

鍾文俊〔貫福建汀州府長汀縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字舜臣，行二，年三十三，八月初四日生〕。曾祖和生，祖清〔典史〕，父正〔教諭〕，母賴氏。具慶下，兄騏，弟文傑〔貢士〕、文倬、文會，娶廖氏。福建鄉試第二名，會試第二百六十名。
translation_en:
Liu Xian, registered in Shehong County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shizi. Second in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinghong, his grandfather Changqi, and his father Chihan; his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fang and his younger brother Jie. His wife was née Yang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Lu, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shiji. Sixth in birth order, he was thirty-nine years old and was born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bifang, his grandfather Guo, and his father Rubai; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dun, Xun (Administration Vice Commissioner in Huguang), Shan, and Bi (璧, Director in the Ministry of Rites). His younger brothers were 𡐤 (reading uncertain [?]) and Bi (坒, a tribute scholar, gongshi). His wife was née Chen. He placed seventy-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hao, registered in Hengyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a household registered for horse-transport boat service and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruqin. Fourth in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sicheng, his grandfather Tiansheng, and his father Gui; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Hong, Hu, and Chao; his younger brothers were Run and Jian. His wife was née Xu. He placed sixty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Wenjun, registered in Changting County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunchen. Second in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hesheng, his grandfather Qing (a Clerk), and his father Zheng (an Instructor); his mother was née Lai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi; his younger brothers were Wenjie (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Wenzhuo, and Wenhui. His wife was née Liao. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄

李雍〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字欽讓，行六，年四十二，十月十五日生〕。曾祖碧玉，祖思敬，父忠亨，母曾氏。慈侍下，兄珎、琳、玭，娶徐氏。福建鄉試第三十七名，會試第二百十五名。

韓大章〔貫湖廣襄陽府襄陽縣，民籍，浙江會稽縣人，國子生，治詩經，字本中，行六，年三十三，十月初八日生〕。曾祖彥達，祖良可〔贈左長史〕，父弼〔左長史〕，前母璩氏〔贈宜人〕，母王氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄邦問〔右布政使〕、質問、博〔典儀〕、善問、明問〔義官〕，娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第十四名，會試第二百二十八名。

徐淮〔貫山東東昌府高唐州武城縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字必東，行一，年二十七，二月十二日生〕。曾祖武，祖青〔巡檢〕，父銓，母張氏。具慶下，弟濟、海、沂、瀛，娶王氏。山東鄉試第三十二名，會試第二百四十名。

胡濂〔貫廣東瓊州府定安縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字宗周，行二，年三十一，二月二十五日生〕。曾祖興祖，祖欽〔判官〕，父瑛〔醫學訓科〕，嫡母陳氏，生母廖氏。具慶下，兄厚，弟深、洛，娶吳氏。廣東鄉試第六十一名，會試第二百五十一名。
translation_en:
Li Yong, courtesy name Qinrang, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Biyu; his grandfather, Sijing; his father, Zhongheng; and his mother, née Zeng. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Zhen, Lin, and Pin, and his wife was née Xu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Dazhang, courtesy name Benzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangyang County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Kuaiji County, Zhejiang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanda; his grandfather, Liangke, posthumously appointed Left Chief Administrator; and his father, Bi, Left Chief Administrator. His father's former wife, née Qu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability (yiren); his mother, née Wang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bangwen, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zhiwen; Bo, Ceremonial Officer; Shanwen; and Mingwen, an honorary official for public beneficence (yiguan). His wife was née Zhang. He ranked fourteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Huai, courtesy name Bidong, was registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu; his grandfather, Qing, a Police Chief; his father, Quan; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji, Hai, Yi, and Ying, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Lian, courtesy name Zongzhou, was registered in a civilian household in Ding'an County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingzu; his grandfather, Qin, an Administrative Assistant; and his father, Ying, an Instructor of Medicine. His legal mother was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Liao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hou, his younger brothers were Shen and Luo, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked sixty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

高遷〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字大用，行三，年四十，九月二十日生〕。曾祖瀚，祖子明，父孟通，母王氏。永感下，兄儒、遂、壽，弟選，娶俞氏。浙江鄉試第八十四名，會試第二百五名。
translation_en:
Wang Xianchen, courtesy name Jingzhi, was registered in an artisan household under the Discipline Office of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An unaffiliated Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenrong, his grandfather Cheng, his father Jin, and his mother née Song. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xianmin and Xianfu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yi, courtesy name Gongzhu, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in birth order, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Weishan, his father Xian, his mother née Jin, and his stepmother née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jie and Lun, the latter a student of astronomy in the Directorate of Astronomy; his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Hong, courtesy name Jiyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congzhou, his grandfather Ying, and his father Zhang, a judicial official of Chizhou Prefecture. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Shao, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Qian, courtesy name Dayong, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third in birth order, was forty years old, and was born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Han, his grandfather Ziming, his father Mengtong, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ru, Sui, and Shou, his younger brother was Xuan, and his wife was née Yu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Tianxi, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Qizhong, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongmei, his grandfather Ding’an, and his father Xuan; his father’s principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tianze, Tianyou, and Tianrui, and his wife was née Wang. He placed seventy-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Tianyou, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jifu, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maoren, his grandfather Yong, and his father Yicheng, Department Magistrate of Shenzhou; his mother was née Wei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tianxing and Tianli, his younger brothers Tianzuo and Tianqi, and his wife was née Hua. He placed sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Xuan, registered in Gaoling County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chaoyong, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhicai, his grandfather Rong, and his father Shu; his mother was née Shang. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother was Yuan and his younger brother Sui; his wife was née Qiu, and his subsequent wife was née Ren. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Zi, registered in Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, in an artisan household, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Congzhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Botong, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor, and his father Ming, an Investigating Censor; his mother was née Zhou, invested with the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guan and his younger brothers Xian, You, and Qu; his wife was née Cai, and his subsequent wife was née Xu. He placed eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Menglong, registered in a civilian household in Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yingling, he was first in birth order, and he was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Nai, an Administration Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi; his father was Jiongran, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his mother, née Guo, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother, née An, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Mengqi and Menglin, both tribute scholars (gongshi), Mengxiong, and Mengpeng. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Kong. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jian, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jujing, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zixin; his grandfather was Yizhen, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father was Yun, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Xue. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Jie, Fu, Ce, Quan, a National University student, and Chi. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Jie, registered in a military household in Jingzhou, Pingliang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Ruqing, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenjing; his grandfather was Ying, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father was Duo, an Honorary Official; his mother was née Shi, and his stepmother was née Meng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living; his younger brothers were Xun, Huai, Ji, Lan, Zhang, and Tong. He married a woman née Wan. He placed tenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Ao, registered in a military household in Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhenzhi, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bogao; his grandfather was Ming, a Registrar in Xiao County; his father was Chun; and his mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased; his elder brother was Jing and his younger brother was Gun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Bian 周昪, courtesy name Qiming, was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered territory, in a military household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guan; his grandfather, Bi; his father, Xun; his mother, née Liang; and his stepmother, née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Bing, and his wife was née Ye. He ranked ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhuang 許莊, courtesy name Dezheng, was registered in Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered territory, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daolong; his grandfather, Mengqing; his father, Yin, Judicial Examiner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother, née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Lin; his younger brother, Xiang, was awaiting selection for official appointment. His wife was née Zhou. He ranked 123rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yun 吳雲, courtesy name Conglong, was registered in Yuhang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the ninth day of the intercalary seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jujing; his grandfather, Si; and his father, Shunmin, Vice Magistrate of Macheng County. His father's former wife was née Zou, and his mother was née Yun. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yingsi. He married a woman née Ren and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Gao. He ranked fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Yue 龍越, courtesy name Dexuan, was registered in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirtieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boqiong; his grandfather, Rufu; his father, He, Assistant Instructor at the Linhuai County Confucian School; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chao, and his younger brother was Qi. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently married a woman née Xiao. He ranked eighty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.
