Hu Yang, registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jinghe; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Fu, and his father Qin, an honorary official for public beneficence; his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Cui. He placed 125th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Ge, registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Pingfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Yi, and his father Chi; his father's former wives were née Xu and née Miao, and his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hui, Registrar of Qingliu County, Mao, Shan, and Shi; his younger brothers were Shu, Ang, and □ [name illegible]. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Zhen, registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Hengfu; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty-three, born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Jun, and his father Zhang; his mother was née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ji, and his younger brothers were Pei, Lei, and Yun. His wife was née Chu. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jin, registered with the Chuzhou Guard in Zhejiang and a native of Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, was a Lishui County school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Demei; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Gucheng, and his father Zongjie; his mother was née Che. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, Gui, and Qi, and his younger brother was Yu. His wife was née Xie. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳玉〔貫直隸沂州衛官籍，揚州府高郵州人，國子生，治詩經，字德卿，行一，年三十九，十月初二日生〕。曾祖景輝，祖茹〔指揮同知〕，父鎬〔指揮同知〕，母奚氏〔封淑人〕。慈侍下，弟瓛、珝，娶孔氏。應天府鄉試第十七名，會試第四十四名。
translation_en:
Zeng Dayou, registered in a military household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shiheng, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sigong, his grandfather Yingtong, and his father Qi, Instructor of Gui County; his father’s former wife and his mother were both née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Xian, School Instructor of Yingzhou, and Dabin, and his younger brother was Daxian. He married a woman née Liu and placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang De, registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a supplementary student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruzhao, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Hong, and his father Chang, an honorary official; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Tang. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Ruxian, Ruliang, Runeng, and Ruming, and his younger brother was Ruduan. He married a woman née Zhou and placed forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Fu, registered with Guangning Left Guard in Liaodong and a native of Jiande County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Liangzuo, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yangzheng, his grandfather Zongkai, a Vice Prefect, and his father Ming; his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Bi and Zhong. He married a woman née Zhang and placed forty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yu, registered in a military officer household of Yizhou Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and a native of Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Deqing, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinghui, his grandfather Ru, a Vice Commander, and his father Gao, also a Vice Commander; his mother was née Xi, granted the title Lady of Gentleness. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Huan and Xu. He married a woman née Kong and placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

侯啓忠〔貫四川叙州府長寧縣竈籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字汝弼，行一，年十八，正月初六日生〕。曾祖璟，祖旺〔知縣〕，父舜臣，母李氏，繼母蔣氏。重慶下，娶劉氏。四川鄉試第三十四名，會試第七十七名。

translation_en:
Li Qin, registered in an official household of Longxiang Guard and a native of Binzhou, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuansu; he was the eldest son, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twentieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Fu, grandfather Min, and father Hui were all company commanders; his mother was née Shi. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Rui, Jian, Yue, Xuan, Kai, Qi, and Zhang, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xing, registered in a civilian household in Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shilong; he was the eldest son, aged forty, and born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Sikao, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Li; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Wang, Xian, Guang, and Zi, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked sixty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Qizhong, registered in a salt-producing household in Changning County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was an additional student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rubi; he was the eldest son, aged eighteen, and born on the sixth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Wang was a county magistrate, and his father was Shunchen; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Jiang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His wife was née Liu. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Kui, registered in a civilian household in Wuyi County, Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianzhang; he was the eldest son, aged thirty, and born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Mao, and his father Zhao, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father's former wife was née Cao and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Duo, and his wife was née Li. He ranked 131st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Pan Yan, courtesy name Shichang, was registered in an officer household of the Jinwu Left Guard and was a native of Xinghua County in Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, a Guard Commander; his grandfather was Fu; his father was Hao, a hereditary officer’s son entitled to wear official cap and girdle; and his mother was née Guo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Qu, and his wife was née Yan. He placed thirteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yang, courtesy name Jianfu, was registered in a civilian household in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuqing; his grandfather was Menghao, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his father was Jiuji; and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qian and Yi, and his wife was née Li. He placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Rui, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered with the Xingzhou Right Agricultural Garrison in Zhili and was a native of Changyi County, Shandong. An added-quota student at the county school of Yutian, Shuntian Prefecture, specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Sheng; his father was Xiong; and his mother was née Dai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gao, his younger brothers were Lian and Zhu, and his wife was née Li. He placed 126th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ran Jizhi, courtesy name Xiaolong, was registered in a civilian household in Li County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, posthumously appointed Registrar; his grandfather was Yi, a Department Vice Magistrate; his father was Cheng, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xuzong, and his wife was née Sheng. He placed forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡昉〔貫浙江紹興府蕭山縣匠籍，國子生，治書經，字啟暘，行八，年三十六，正月十九日生〕。曾祖子良，祖仕能，父永芳，母湯氏。慈侍下，兄暠、杲，弟晨，娶屠氏。浙江鄉試第四十八名，會試第一百五十九名。

顧守元〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字明善，行一，年三十四，八月二十七日生〕。曾祖有終〔義官〕，祖岑〔義官〕，父鉞，母俞氏。慈侍下，娶龔氏。應天府鄉試第八十三名，會試第二百十三名。
translation_en:
Li Jin, registered in a civilian household in Qian’an County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zongqian, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-three sui, born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Lin, and his father You, Assistant Instructor at the Haizhou Guard School; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Zheng; his grandfather and both parents were living; his elder brother was Rui and his younger brothers Jin, Qian, Yu, Yin, and Liu; he married a woman née Xu and placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tianfu, registered in a military household in Jiaocheng County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ningdao, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei, his grandfather Desheng, and his father Jing, a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his mother was née Gao; his grandfather and both parents were living; his younger brothers were Tianbi and Tianxi; he married a woman née Tan and placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Fang, registered in an artisan household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Qiyang, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was thirty-six sui, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang, his grandfather Shineng, and his father Yongfang; his mother was née Tang; his mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Gao 暠 and Gao 杲, and his younger brother was Chen; he married a woman née Tu and placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Shouyuan, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mingshan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Youzhong and grandfather Cen both held the honorary title of Righteous Official; his father was Yue and his mother née Yu; his mother was living and his father deceased; he married a woman née Gong and placed eighty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
黃鑅〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣，軍籍，府學生，治易經，字于宣，行三，年三十二，四月十二日生〕。曾祖顯祖，祖景燦，父齊，母蔡氏，繼母董氏。具慶下，兄銘〔同科進士〕、鏻，弟鉚、銓，娶楊氏。福建鄉試第二十六名，會試第一百五十五名。

王良臣〔貫河南開封府陳州，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字汝隣，行一，年三十八，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖弘義，祖哲，父璋，母高氏，繼母徐氏、戚氏。重慶下，弟良相、良弼、良士，娶盧氏。河南鄉試第二十八名，會試第二十一名。

曹恕〔貫順天府霸州，軍籍，州學增廣生，治書經，字本忠，行一，年二十六，八月二十七日生〕。曾祖顯〔監察御史〕，祖璉，父紀〔白水主簿〕，前母高氏，母楊氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，弟態、恱、恩、憲，娶于氏。順天府鄉試第一百八名，會試第一百五十名。

黎堯卿〔貫四川忠州守禦千戶所籍，本州人，國子生，治詩經，字廷表，行四，年三十六，十月二十二日生〕。曾祖從義，祖茂清〔贈經歷〕，父瑄〔南京錦衣衛經歷〕，母李氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母龍氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄堯佐，弟堯吉、堯官、堯士，娶牟氏。四川鄉試第六十一名，會試第三百名。
translation_en:
Huang Heng 黃鑅, courtesy name Yuxuan, was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianzu; his grandfather, Jingcan; and his father, Qi. His mother was née Cai, and his stepmother née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ming〔a jinshi of the same examination cohort〕and Lin; his younger brothers were Mao and Quan. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Liangchen 王良臣, courtesy name Rulin, was registered in Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hongyi; his grandfather, Zhe; and his father, Zhang. His mother was née Gao, and his successive stepmothers were née Xu and née Qi. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Liangxiang, Liangbi, and Liangshi. He married a woman née Lu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Shu 曹恕, courtesy name Benzhong, was registered in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, in a military household. An additional student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian〔Investigating Censor〕; his grandfather, Lian; and his father, Ji〔Registrar of Baishui County〕. His father's former wife was née Gao, his mother née Yang, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tai [?], Yue, En, and Xian. He married a woman née Yu. He placed 108th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yaoqing 黎堯卿, courtesy name Tingbiao, was registered with the Zhongzhou Defense Thousand-household Office in Sichuan and was a native of Zhongzhou. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congyi; his grandfather, Maoqing〔posthumously granted the title of Office Manager〕; and his father, Xuan〔Office Manager of the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard〕. His mother was née Li〔posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren)〕, and his stepmother née Long〔granted the title of Lady (ruren)〕. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yaozuo; his younger brothers were Yaoji, Yaoguan, and Yaoshi. He married a woman née Mou. He placed sixty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王崇文〔貫山東兖州府曹州曹縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字叔武，行三，年二十六，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖導，祖蘭〔巡檢，贈布政〕，父珣〔河南右參政〕，母李氏〔贈恭人〕，繼母孔氏、苗氏〔封恭人〕。□□下，兄崇儒、崇高、崇仁，弟崇獻、崇讓、崇禮、崇宥、崇儉、崇素，娶劉氏。□□鄉試第十二名，會試第一百四十七名。
translation_en:
Yao Hao 姚昊, courtesy name Wenda, was registered in a military household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a native of Min County. An additional student at the Min County school, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he ranked third in his family, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Gui, and his father Xian; his mother was née Liu. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Sheng, and his wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lian 劉璉, courtesy name Tingmei, was registered in a medical household in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he ranked fourth in his family, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yanqing was a Medical Officer; his grandfather Mengqi was a Physician in the Imperial Medical Service. His father was Futian; his father's former wife was née Zhuang, and his mother was née Miao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ying, Yu, and Zhang. He married a woman née Yao and subsequently a woman née Fan. He placed eighty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xin 黃信, courtesy name Junshi, was registered with the Central Guard of the Rear Military Commission and was a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian. An additional student at the Shuntian Prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he ranked first in his family, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Quan, and his father Zhong; his mother was née Cao. His father alone was still living. His wife was née Yang. He placed fifty-first in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chongwen 王崇文, courtesy name Shuwu, was registered in a civilian household in Cao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he ranked third in his family, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dao; his grandfather Lan was a Police Chief, posthumously awarded the title of Provincial Administration Commissioner. His father Xun was Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan. His mother, née Li, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Respect; his stepmothers were née Kong and née Miao, with the annotation “granted the title of Lady of Respect.” His parental survival status is illegible [?]. His elder brothers were Chongru, Chonggao, and Chongren; his younger brothers were Chongxian, Chongrang, Chongli, Chongyou, Chongjian, and Chongsu. His wife was née Liu. He placed twelfth in the Provincial Examination for an illegible location [?] and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

譚玉瑞〔貫湖廣長沙府茶陵州軍籍，國子生，治易經，字雅祥，行三，年三十六，正月十四日生〕。曾祖子文，祖世烈，父錫〔遇例冠帶〕，母劉氏。具慶下，兄雅音、雅韶，弟雅淵、雅祺，娶彭氏，繼娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第六十名，會試第九十三名。

馬慶〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字善徵，行三，年三十五，九月初二日生〕。曾祖德，祖克章，父顥，母楊氏。具慶下，兄恩、惠，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第一百四名，會試第四十一名。
translation_en:
Hu En, courtesy name Yuncheng, was registered in a military household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; eighth in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Zhi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi; his father was Qian, and his mother was née Fang. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Fu, an Imperial University student, Xing, and Huan; his younger brothers were Kai, Xun and Zao, both tribute scholars, Mao, De, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), and Qing. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Die, courtesy name Siwen, was registered in a military household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; sixth in birth order, he was aged forty-two and was born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Nanshou; his grandfather was Chao, an Examiner; and his father was Yingzhen, an Assistant Commissioner. His father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xu, an Assistant Prefect; Shao, a Secretary; Shou, a District Magistrate; Shan; and Hui, a Grand Coordinator. His younger brothers were Zhan, Chief Minister of a Branch Court of the Imperial Stud, and Tong. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventy-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Yurui, courtesy name Yaxiang, was registered in a military household in Chaling Subprefecture, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; third in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziwen; his grandfather was Shilie; his father was Xi, granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yayin and Yashao, and his younger brothers were Yayuan and Yaqi. His wife was née Peng; he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He placed sixtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Qing, courtesy name Shanzheng, was registered in an artisan household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; third in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Kezhang; his father was Hao; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were En and Hui, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 104th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

江師古〔貫湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字克永，行一，年三十六，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖朝宗〔通判〕，祖瀾，父旭，母李氏。慈侍下，弟述古、學古、蘊古、信古，娶唐氏，繼娶李氏。湖廣鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百四十三名。

陳熺〔貫福建福州府閩縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字師晦，行四，年三十，九月初十日生〕。曾祖環，祖浩，父樂，母黃氏，繼母張氏。嚴侍下，兄煒，娶余氏。福建鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百九名。
translation_en:
Su Xin, registered in Yong'an County, Yanping Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongfu, he was sixth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengsan, his grandfather Zigong, his father Jishi, and his mother née Lin; both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenmao and his younger brother Wenquan; his wife was née Wu. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xiyan, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yuanfu, he was fifth in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Kuan and grandfather Xuan were tribute scholars; his father Yin was Director of the County School in Xinchang. His father's former wife was née Jiang, and his mother was née Wang; his father alone was living. His elder brothers were Xitai, an honorary official, Xixian, Xixian (希憲), and Xiwen; his younger brother was Xizeng, and his wife was née Yu. He placed seventy-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Shigu, registered in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Keyong, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Chaozong was an Assistant Prefect, his grandfather was Lan, his father Xu, and his mother née Li; his mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Shugu, Xuegu, Yungu, and Xingu; he married a woman née Tang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed eighty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xi, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shihui, he was fourth in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Hao, his father Le, his mother née Huang, and his stepmother née Zhang; his father alone was living. His elder brother was Wei, and his wife was née Yu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gui Zhao, courtesy name Shiqin, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked forty-third in family order and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongru, a Compiler; his grandfather was Chengxue; his father was Jing; and his mother was née Zhao. His mother alone was living. His elder brother Zan was an Assistant Instructor at the Xuyi County School, and his younger brother was Gao. He married a woman née Ye and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Tu, courtesy name Konggui, was registered in a civilian household in Yangshuo County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huaiji; his grandfather was Longguang; and his father was Sheng, a Registrar of Huizhou Prefecture. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bi and Xi, and he married a woman née Zhou. He placed fiftieth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jin, courtesy name Weiqing, was registered in an officer household of the Xi'an Rear Guard, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-five, born on the third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, Chief Military Commissioner of the Right; his grandfather was Ying, a Pacification Officer posthumously granted the title of Commander; and his father was Min, a County Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jing, and he married a woman née Guo. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Xiong, courtesy name Wenying, was registered in a civilian household in Xun County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixian; his grandfather was Rong; his father was Bin; and his mother was née Lu. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Jie and Ren, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventy-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
鮑璋，貫山東青州府壽光縣，竈籍，國子生，治春秋，字重器，行一，年三十八，八月二十八日生。曾祖友直，祖祥，父通，嫡母栁氏，生母范氏。慈侍下，弟璘、琨、瑜、珽、瓚、仝，娶丁氏。山東鄉試第四名，會試第一百三十四名。

何垕，貫江西建昌府新城縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字朝舉，行三，年四十，三月初一日生。曾祖澄〔禮科給事中〕，祖撗〔左長史〕，父燮〔貢士〕，母涂氏。永感下，兄璽、塏，娶江氏。江西鄉試第七十四名，會試第一百十六名。

秦文，貫浙江台州府臨海縣，軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字從簡，行十，年二十九，十月十六日生。曾祖良玉，祖宗傅，父彥彬，母董氏，繼母吳氏。具慶下，兄章、裕，弟禮、祺、祹、武，娶姚氏。浙江鄉試第一名，會試第一百八十名。

焦澤，貫直隸廣平府永年縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字克濟，行二，年三十，十一月二十三日生。曾祖欽〔知縣〕，祖迪〔太原府經歷〕，父祺〔貢士〕，母鄭氏。慈侍下，兄溥，弟淵、濟，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百二名，會試第一百三十八名。
translation_en:
Bao Zhang 鮑璋 was registered in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a salt-producing household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zhongqi, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-eight, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youzhi, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Tong; his legal mother was née Liu and his birth mother née Fan. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Lin, Kun, Yu, Ting, Zan, and Tong. He married a woman née Ding. He placed fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Hou 何垕 was registered in Xincheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household, and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Chaoju, and he ranked third in birth order. He was forty, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Cheng was a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; his grandfather Heng 撗 was a Left Chief Administrator; his father Xie was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His mother was née Tu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xi and Kai. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Wen 秦文 was registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household, and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Congjian, and he ranked tenth in birth order. He was twenty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liangyu, his grandfather Zongfu, and his father Yanbin; his mother was née Dong and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhang and Yu, and his younger brothers Li, Qi, Tao, and Wu. He married a woman née Yao. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiao Ze 焦澤 was registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Keji, and he ranked second in birth order. He was thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Qin was a District Magistrate; his grandfather Di was Registrar of Taiyuan Prefecture; his father Qi was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His mother was née Zheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Pu, and his younger brothers Yuan and Ji. He married a woman née Li. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Ying, courtesy name Dengzhi, was from Fei County, Yizhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and belonged to a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, Clerk of Haining County; his grandfather was An; his father was Jian; and his mother was née Peng. His parents and grandparent(s) were living. He was betrothed to a woman née Song. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lin, courtesy name Shiyu, was from Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongxian; his grandfather was Mengzhong; his father was Xidao, Postmaster of Xiapi; and his mother was née Ye. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yin, Yun, and Ni. He married a woman née Sun and subsequently women née Yang and née Yao. He ranked thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qiong, courtesy name Guoyong, was from Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and belonged to a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxian; his grandfather was Shaoliang; his father was Shurang; and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhao. He ranked seventy-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Rumei, courtesy name Xida, was from Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather was Cheng; his father was Tianyu; his mother was née Zhou; and his stepmother was née Lin. His father and stepmother were living. He married a woman née Lin. He ranked fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Jun, courtesy name Keyong, was registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Shiqi, his father Da, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ren, Zuo, and Jie, and his younger brothers Yan and Kan; his wife was née Xu. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Rujing, courtesy name Anzhi, was registered in Weinan County, Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, Registrar of Langzhong County; his grandfather was Hao; and his father was Long, Prefect of Jining Subprefecture. His mother was née Ren and his stepmother née Shi; both parents were living. His elder brother was Runing, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yue, courtesy name Weisong, was registered in Wuhe County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Tong, and his father Zhiqian; the text lists his mother as née Zhu and also his mother as née Wang [?]. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shan, and his younger brother Lun was a Medical Instructor in a medical school; his wife was née Liang. He placed 120th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Ding, courtesy name Zhongqi, was registered in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in an artisan household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congli, his grandfather Yong, his father Ming, his mother née Zhou, and his stepmother née Xiao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Zi, and his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
歐陽介〔貫江西吉安府安福縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字勗辨，行十二，年三十五，四月初二日生〕。曾祖孟武，祖脩已，父寧〔含山知縣〕，前母劉氏，母顏氏。永感下，兄勗重、勗遠、勗堅，弟淑、定、宋，娶王氏。江西鄉試第二十四名，會試第五十八名。

李濬〔貫直隸鳳陽府鳳陽縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字文淵，行一，年四十，二月十二日生〕。曾祖通，祖誠，父瑋〔鹿邑縣學教諭〕，母陳氏。慈侍下，弟溥、澍，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第二十四名。

袁仕〔貫湖廣襄陽府棗陽縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字良輔，行二，年二十九，八月十八日生〕。曾祖真，祖顯〔贈同知〕，父盛〔黎平知府〕，母馮氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄傅〔貢士〕，弟備〔義官〕、偉、儒、伯，娶施氏。湖廣鄉試第十八名，會試第一百四十九名。

居達〔貫順天府大興縣匠籍，府學生，治易經，字德亨，行二，年三十，九月二十日生〕。曾祖禮，祖子誠，父福，母黃氏。慈侍下，兄勝，弟榮，娶燕氏。順天府鄉試第一百十名，會試第一百三十名。
translation_en:
Ouyang Jie, registered in a military household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xubian; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Mengwu; his grandfather, Xiuyi; and his father, Ning, Magistrate of Hanshan County. His father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xuzhong, Xuyuan, and Xujian; his younger brothers were Shu, Ding, and Song [?]. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jun, registered in a military household in Fengyang County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenyuan; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty, and was born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Cheng; and his father, Wei, Instructor at the Luyi County Confucian School. His mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Pu and Shu. His wife was née Zhang. He placed ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Shi, registered in a military household in Zaoyang County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Liangfu; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Xian, posthumously granted the title of Vice Prefect; and his father, Sheng, Prefect of Liping. His mother was née Feng, granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fu, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Bei, an honorary official for contributions to public causes, Wei, Ru, and Bo. His wife was née Shi. He placed eighteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ju Da, registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the prefectural Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Deheng; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty, and was born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Zicheng; and his father, Fu. His mother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Sheng, and his younger brother was Rong. His wife was née Yan. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
陳珀〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，山東堂邑縣學教諭，治書經，字珍之，行一，年三十二，十二月十二日生〕。曾祖乾初，祖孟敬，父順元，母黃氏。嚴侍下，弟瑚、璵、瑠，娶郭氏。福建鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百二十二名。

任文獻〔貫山東兖州府沂州郯城縣，軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字國光，行一，年三十八，十一月十二日生〕。曾祖仲禮，祖貴，父福〔聽選官〕，母王氏，繼母田氏。慈侍下，弟文育、文賔、文齊、文德、文思、聰、章，娶咸氏。山東鄉試第八名，會試第二百四十七名。

湯佐〔貫四川潼川州安岳縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字時衡，行四，年二十八，十月十八日生〕。曾祖希韶，祖瑀，父煥新，母程氏。重慶下，兄誥、輅、孜、相，弟輻，娶胡氏。四川鄉試第九名，會試第一百九十一名。

李祚〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字光世，行三十八，年四十五，七月十三日生〕。曾祖獻誠〔贈主事〕，祖應庚〔知府，贈中議大夫、賛治尹〕，父直〔保寧知府〕，母徐氏〔封安人〕。永感下，兄福〔進士〕、祿、禎、祥〔訓術〕、祈、礽、裸〔義官〕、禨，娶夏氏。江西鄉試第三名，會試第三十九名。
translation_en:
Chen Po, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was Instructor at the county school of Tangyi, Shandong. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhenzhi. First in birth order, he was thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qianchu, his grandfather Mengjing, his father Shunyuan, and his mother née Huang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Hu, Yu, and Liu; his wife was née Guo. He placed fifty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Wenxian, registered in Tancheng County, Yizhou Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Guoguang. First in birth order, he was thirty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhongli, his grandfather Gui, and his father Fu, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Tian. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Wenyu, Wenbin, Wenqi, Wende, Wensi, Cong, and Zhang; his wife was née Xian. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Zuo, registered in Anyue County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shiheng. Fourth in birth order, he was twenty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xishao, his grandfather Yu, his father Huanxin, and his mother née Cheng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Gao, Lu, Zi, and Xiang; his younger brother was Fu. His wife was née Hu. He placed ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zuo, registered in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Guangshi. Thirty-eighth in birth order, he was forty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Xiancheng was posthumously appointed a Bureau Secretary. His grandfather Yinggeng was a Prefect, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Deliberation (zhongyi dafu) and Governor Assisting in Administration (zanzhi yin). His father Zhi was Prefect of Baoning, and his mother, née Xu, was granted the title Lady of Repose. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); Lu; Zhen; Xiang, an Instructor in Daoist Arts; Qi; Reng; Luo [?], an honorary official; and Ji. His wife was née Xia. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫瑞〔貫順天府東安縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字季禎，行一，年三十二，二月二十二日生〕。曾祖彥禮，祖昇〔府倉大使〕，父進〔義官〕，母徐氏，繼母吳氏。具慶下，兄琳〔聽選官〕、珍、璁，弟瑾、璋、玥、玠、珂，娶胡氏。順天府鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百七十八名。

廖漢〔貫湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字天章，行一，年四十一，六月十三日生〕。曾祖從信〔景東衛經歷〕，祖淵，父俊〔漢州學正〕，母黃氏。具慶下，兄滋〔聽選官〕、海〔義官〕，弟瀠、洪、應辰、溫、滂、濂、瀚，娶江氏。湖廣鄉試第十四名，會試第八十九名。

徐永〔貫河南開封府鈞州軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字昌齡，行一，年二十八，七月十二日生〕。曾祖原貴，祖明善〔知州〕，父中孚〔義官〕，母婁氏，繼母張氏。具慶下，弟亨，娶王氏。河南鄉試第五十二名，會試第二百八十七名。

姚學禮〔貫府軍前衛籍，四川巴縣人，儒士，治易經，字以立，行一，年三十四，閏十月三十日生〕。曾祖文，祖常，父伯高，母舒氏。具慶下，娶萬氏。順天府鄉試第一名，會試第一百二十一名。
translation_en:
Sun Rui, courtesy name Jizhen, was registered in a military household in Dong’an County, Shuntian Prefecture; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yanli; his grandfather, Sheng, was Commissioner of a prefectural granary; his father, Jin, held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Service; his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lin, an official awaiting selection for appointment, Zhen, and Cong; his younger brothers were Jin, Zhang, Yue, Jie, and Ke. He married a woman née Hu. He placed eighty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Han, courtesy name Tianzhang, was registered in a military household in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged forty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Congxin, was Registrar of Jingdong Guard; his grandfather was Yuan; his father, Jun, was an Instructor at the Hanzhou prefectural school; his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zi, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and Hai, who held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Service; his younger brothers were Ying, Hong, Yingchen, Wen, Pang, Lian, and Han. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed fourteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yong, courtesy name Changling, was registered in a military household in Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuangui; his grandfather, Mingshan, was a Prefect; his father, Zhongfu, held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Service; his mother was née Lou, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Heng, and he married a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Xueli, courtesy name Yili, was registered with the Front Guard of the Imperial Retinue and was a native of Ba County, Sichuan; he was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirtieth day of the intercalary tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather was Chang; his father was Bogao; his mother was née Shu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Wan. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Bao 劉袌, courtesy name Tingyan, was registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Yancheng was posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief; his grandfather Daoli was a Registrar and was likewise posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief. His father Fu was retired Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Zhou, was posthumously granted the title of Lady; his birth mother was née Peng. His father and birth mother were both living. His elder brothers were Tingming, a Company Commander, and Pou, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Yi, Jiong, and Biao. His wife was née Wu. He ranked eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Xi 曹璽, courtesy name Tingyu, was registered in a military household in Lan County, Kelan Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Youxian, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Chen; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His wife was née Liu. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yu 張彧, courtesy name Wenhan, was registered in a civilian household in Yuanshi County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Siyi, his grandfather Qin, and his father Shen; his mother was née He. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Tong and Hu. His wife was née Li. He ranked seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Qing 黃清, courtesy name Yuanjie, was registered in an artisan household of the Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Kunshan County, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhong, his grandfather Sicong, and his father Cong; his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cheng, and his younger brothers were Pu and Liu. His wife was née Yue. He ranked 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Huaide, courtesy name Duanben, was registered in a military household in Xinjin County, Chongqing Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather, Zitian; his father, Yang; and his mother, née Gu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Huaihou, Huairen, and Huaiyi. His wife was née Zhu. He ranked eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zhixue, courtesy name Xunfu, was registered with Pengcheng Guard and was a native of Changsha County, Huguang. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shou; his grandfather, Fusheng; and his father, Chun. His father's former wives were née Liu and née Luo; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang. He ranked twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü You, courtesy name Guobi, was registered in a civilian household in Deping County, Dezhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Lu; and his father, Shao. His father's principal wife was née Ding, and his birth mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were An and Zuo (a student of the Imperial University); his younger brothers were Wei, Shao, Xiu, Yi, Pei, and Ji. His wife was née Kang. He ranked fortieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Sui, courtesy name Decheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was eighth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xuncheng (honorarily granted the title of Investigating Censor); his grandfather, Menghong (granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations); his father, Xincun (Commissioner of a Transport Office); and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were En, Xun, Zhao, Huang, and Duan; his younger brothers were Ming and Wei. His wife was née Yang. He ranked third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Wenda, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Side. Fourth among his brothers, he was thirty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cai, his grandfather Lei, and his father Sheng, a tribute student; his mother was née Zheng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Xiang, Chong, and Yi, and his younger brother was Wenming. His wife was née Ye. He placed thirty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Gao, registered in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shizhao. Third among his brothers, he was thirty years old and was born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinghua, his grandfather Xian, Left Chief Secretary, and his father Tai, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan. His father's former wife, née Wang, had been posthumously awarded the title Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Hu, had been granted the same title; his stepmother was née Xiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ang, an Instructor of Medicine, and Dan, and his younger brother was Chang. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Huan, registered in Shanyang County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was Instructor at the Pingshan County Confucian school in Zhiding Prefecture [?]. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Wenming. First among his brothers, he was forty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menglin, his grandfather Weide, and his father Benda; his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Wenzhao. His first wife was née Huang, and his subsequent wife was née Bi. He placed 134th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yongcai, registered in Pengshan County, Mei Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jingji. First among his brothers, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shitong, his grandfather Zixiu, and his father Lun; his mother was née Zhao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Yongzhong, and his wife was née Tang. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Que 石確, courtesy name Dejian, was registered in a civilian household in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youzhong; his grandfather, Ding; his father, Ying; and his mother, née Deng. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Gao. He placed sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Tai 高臺, courtesy name Juxian, was registered in a salt-producing household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was twelfth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benzhong, Vice Prefect of Guilin Prefecture; his grandfather, Zongxi, an honorary official; and his father, Guicong. His father's former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Shen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Tang and Shi, and his younger brothers were Hou and Sai. He married a woman née Lu. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tan 徐潭, courtesy name Rurong, was registered in an artisan household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the tenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Derun; his grandfather, Wenzhi, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; and his father, Min, Prefect of Guangnan Prefecture. His mother, née Lu, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Hao, and his younger brothers were Hong, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and He, an honorary official. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently another woman née Chen. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hui Long 惠隆, courtesy name Congdao, was registered with the Wuxiang Right Guard and was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongmao; his grandfather, Qian; and his father, Da, a Company Commander. His mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Luan. He was betrothed to a woman née Jiang. He placed 121st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Qing, registered in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a commoner household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruyin; he ranked tenth in family birth order, was twenty-nine sui, and was born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bozhong, his grandfather Jihong, and his father Shou, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his mother was née Liao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Mei and subsequently a woman née Lao. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhe, registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xixian; he ranked eleventh in family birth order, was thirty-eight sui, and was born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rongqing, his grandfather Wenshou, and his father Bosheng, an honorary official; his father's former wife was née Du, and his mother was née Ai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yonggang, Yougang, and Ligang. He married a woman née Wei. He placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Yan, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingzhan; he ranked second in family birth order, was thirty-three sui, and was born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weimo, his grandfather Jun, and his father Long; his mother was née Dong. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Luan, and his younger brothers were Kun and Song. He married a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Tian, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a commoner household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Hongzai; he ranked first in family birth order, was thirty-seven sui, and was born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongjin, his grandfather Ju, and his father Fuyang; his mother was née Zhuang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Mai and Ye. He married a woman née Wu. He placed fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Zhe, registered in Liaozhou, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zongdai, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather Gang, and his father Qian, a County Magistrate; his mother was née Fan, both parents were living, his elder brother was Huai, his younger brothers were Yan and Gan, and his wife was née Zhao; he placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Shao, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered territory, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xingzhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yixin, his grandfather Tingyu, and his father Lan; his mother was née Qian, both parents were living, his younger brother was Wu, and his wife was née Qian; he placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ruqing, registered in Zhongmou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Lianfu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhu, his grandfather Han, County Magistrate of Rui'an, and his father Xuan, an honorary official for public benefaction; his mother was née Zhang, both parents were deceased, his younger brother was Ruhong, and his wife was née Zhang; he placed thirtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shiheng, registered in Rongcheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shiyong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Su, his grandfather Jing, posthumously granted the title of Guard Registrar, and his father Teng, granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; his mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Zhao, his father and stepmother were living, his younger brothers were Shiqing, Shixiang, Shideng, and Shixian, and he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhang; he placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zhen 王震, courtesy name Weiyuan, was registered in Xingtai County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingxian; his grandfather, Xi, was Subprefect of Pingdu Subprefecture; and his father was Zheng. His father’s former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wen, Zhang, and Man, and his younger brothers were Ni and Ting. His wife was née Hao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xiao 張斆, courtesy name Shixue, was registered with the Dali Guard in Yunnan and was a native of Jiaxing County, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingfu; his grandfather, Xi, was posthumously awarded the title of Bureau Director; and his father, Zheng, was Prefect of Jianning. His mother, née Lü, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brother, Min, was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brother was Che. His wife was née Lu. He placed fourth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟三代
而下論守成之君
必以漢文帝為首
史稱其時海内殷
富興於禮義斷獄
===
數百幾致刑措朕
嘗慕之不知文帝
何脩而能得此考
之當時或賜民田
租之半或盡除之

punctuated: 皇帝制曰：「朕惟三代而下，論守成之君，必以漢文帝為首。史稱其時海内殷富，興於禮義，斷獄數百，幾致刑措。朕嘗慕之，不知文帝何脩而能得此？考之當時，或賜民田租之半，或盡除之……」
translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: “I consider that, since the Three Dynasties, any discussion of rulers who preserved their inherited realm must place Emperor Wen of Han first. The histories state that in his time all within the seas enjoyed abundance and prosperity, rites and righteousness flourished, and only several hundred criminal cases were adjudicated, so that punishments could almost be set aside. I have long admired this, but do not know what Emperor Wen cultivated to achieve it. Examining his time, I find that he sometimes remitted half the people's land tax, and sometimes abolished it altogether…

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
殷富之效蓋出於
此然貢助徹之法
雖三代亦所常行
而況於漢乎使除
田租則當時宗廟
===
之祭祀百官之俸
給四夷之征伐皆
不可已者將何以
給用度乎仰惟
皇祖肇造區夏罔不

殷富之效盖出於
此然貢助徹之法
雖三代亦所常行
而况於漢乎使除
田租則當時宗廟
===

給四夷之征伐皆

punctuated: 殷富之效蓋出於此。然貢助徹之法，雖三代亦所常行，而況於漢乎？使除田租，則當時宗廟之祭祀、百官之俸給、四夷之征伐，皆不可已者，將何以給用度乎？仰惟皇祖肇造區夏，罔不
translation_en: …The resulting prosperity presumably arose from this. Yet the gong, zhu, and che systems of taxation were regularly practiced even under the Three Dynasties; how much more so under the Han? If the land tax were abolished, how could expenditures have been met for ancestral temple sacrifices, salaries for the officials, and campaigns against the peoples of the four quarters—none of which could be discontinued? Reverently reflecting upon Our imperial ancestor’s founding of the realm, there were none who did not…

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
臣服百二十餘年
以來生齒益繁疆
域益廣非前代所
及今歲郡縣上版
籍于戶部其數具
===
存可謂庶矣休養
生息之餘宜其富
而可教也然聞閭
巷田野之間不免
凍餒無聊之歎且
alt_text:
臣服百二十餘年
以来生齒益繁疆
域益廣非前代所
及今歲郡縣上版
籍于戶部其數具
===
存可謂庶矣休養
生息之餘宜其富
而可教也然閭閻
巷田野之間不免
凍餒無聊之歎且
punctuated: 臣服。百二十餘年以來，生齒益繁，疆域益廣，非前代所及。今歲郡縣上版籍于戶部，其數具存，可謂庶矣。休養生息之餘，宜其富而可教也。然聞閭巷田野之間，不免凍餒無聊之歎，且
translation_en: …submitted as subjects. Over the past hundred and twenty-odd years, the population has steadily increased and the territory steadily expanded, beyond what previous dynasties attained. This year, the prefectures and counties submitted their population registers to the Ministry of Revenue; the figures are all on record. The people may indeed be called numerous. After a period of rest and recuperation, they ought to be prosperous and ready to receive moral instruction. Yet we hear that in the lanes and countryside, there are still laments over cold, hunger, and lack of a livelihood. Moreover…

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
頃因水旱河決之
患尤多流移失業
之人安在其為富
也是以勸諭雖切
而循理者尚少赦
宥雖頻而犯法者
愈甚又安在其為
可教也夫衣食不
足則禮義不興而
民輕犯乎刑辟亦
alt_text:
頃因水旱河決之
患尤多流移失業
之人安在其爲富
也是以勸諭雖切
而循理者尚少赦
===
宥雖頻而犯法者
愈甚又安在其爲
可教也夫衣食不
足則禮義不興而
民輕犯乎刑辟亦
punctuated: 頃因水旱河決之患，尤多流移失業之人，安在其為富也？是以勸諭雖切，而循理者尚少；赦宥雖頻，而犯法者愈甚，又安在其為可教也？夫衣食不足，則禮義不興，而民輕犯乎刑辟，亦……
translation_en: …recently, owing to floods, droughts, and breaches of river embankments, especially many people have been displaced and lost their livelihoods. How, then, can they be called prosperous? Thus, although exhortations are earnest, those who follow moral principles remain few; although pardons are frequent, violations of the law grow ever more serious. How, then, can the people be considered ready to receive moral instruction? When food and clothing are insufficient, ritual propriety and righteousness do not flourish, and the people readily transgress the penal laws; this, too, …

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
勢之所必至者其
將何以處之蓋古
之御天下者既庶
必有富之之術既
富必有教之之方
===
特患不能舉行之
耳朕承
祖宗鴻業圖惟治道
每有志於隆古帝
王之盛不但文帝
alt_text:
勢之所必至者其
將何以處之蓋古
之御天下者旣庶
必有富之之術旣
富必有教之之方
===
特患不能舉行之
耳朕承
祖宗鴻業圖惟治道
每有志於隆古帝
王之盛不但文帝
punctuated:
勢之所必至者，其將何以處之？蓋古之御天下者，既庶必有富之之術，既富必有教之之方，特患不能舉行之耳。
朕承祖宗鴻業，圖惟治道，每有志於隆古帝王之盛，不但文帝
translation_en:
…is also an inevitable consequence of these circumstances. How, then, should this be addressed? Those who governed all under Heaven in antiquity, once the people were numerous, necessarily had means to enrich them; once they were prosperous, they necessarily had methods to educate them. The only concern was the inability to put these into practice.
I have inherited the magnificent undertaking of my imperial ancestors and ponder the way of good government. My constant aspiration is to attain the flourishing rule of the emperors and kings of high antiquity, and not merely that of Emperor Wen…

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
而已爾諸生抱道
而来將見於用其
於庶富教三者先
後本末凡古人之
成效今日之急務
===
悉心以陳朕將親
覽焉
弘治六年三月十五日
alt_text:
而已爾諸生抱道
而来將見於用其
於庶富教三者先
後本末凡古人之
成效今日之急務
悉心以陳朕將親
覽焉
===
弘治六年三月十五日
punctuated:
而已。爾諸生抱道而来，將見於用，其於庶富教三者先後本末，凡古人之成效、今日之急務，悉心以陳，朕將親覽焉。
弘治六年三月十五日。
translation_en:
…alone. You candidates have come bearing the Way and are about to enter service. Concerning the three matters of increasing the population, enriching it, and educating it—their proper sequence and their fundamental and subsidiary aspects—set forth with full care both the proven achievements of the ancients and the urgent tasks of the present day. I shall personally read your responses.
Fifteenth day of the third month of the sixth year of Hongzhi (1493).

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
臣毛澄
臣對臣聞有天下者必有以安天下必思所以率天
下蓋天下之民固人君之所當安而民之所以安非
人君以一身為天下先不可也故必在我者無所厲
乎民乃可以富民於既庶之餘又必在我者有足法
於民乃可以教民於既富之後庶且富焉則立之者
固而民無不獲其所富且教焉則道之者至而民罔
或干於正此古之帝王所以躋一世於阜成作百王
之模範而三代以下若漢之文帝其亦可謂庶幾乎
此焉者矣欽惟
===
皇帝陛下撫盈成之運當鼎盛之年聰睿有臨得之天縱
日月所照悉歸版圖所謂能致之資必致之勢蓋兼
而有之矣如臣等一介草茅未諳治體迂疎之論豈
足以仰裨
德業之隆而
明命下臨天章煥爛詢及乎庶富教之事真誠懇惻曾
無一毫自大自滿之心臣伏而讀之有以見
陛下克讓如唐堯好生若虞舜足以荷
天眷之休足以承
祖業之重足以為億兆之
alt_text:
臣毛澄
臣對臣聞有天下者當心有以安天下必思所以率天
下蓋天下之民固人君之所當安而民之所以安非
人君以一身為天下先不可也故必在我者無所厲
乎民乃可以富民於既庶之餘又必在我者有足法
於民乃可以教民於既富之後庶且富焉則立之者
固而民無不獲其所富且教焉則道之者至而民罔
或干於正此古之帝王所以躋一世於阜成作百王
之模範而三代以下若漢之文帝其亦可謂庶幾乎
此焉者矣欽惟
===
皇帝陛下撫盈成之運當鼎盛之年聰睿有臨得之天縱
日月所照悉歸版圖所謂能致之資必致之勢蓋無
而有之矣如臣等一介草茅未諳治體迂疏之論豈
足以仰裨
德業之隆而
明命下臨天章煥爛詢及乎庶富教之事真誠懇惻曾
無一毫自大自滿之心臣伏而讀之有以見
陛下克讓如唐堯好生若虞舜足以荷
天眷之休足以承
祖業之重足以為億兆之
punctuated:
臣毛澄。
臣對：臣聞有天下者，必有以安天下，必思所以率天下。蓋天下之民，固人君之所當安，而民之所以安，非人君以一身為天下先不可也。故必在我者無所厲乎民，乃可以富民於既庶之餘；又必在我者有足法於民，乃可以教民於既富之後。庶且富焉，則立之者固，而民無不獲其所；富且教焉，則道之者至，而民罔或干於正。此古之帝王所以躋一世於阜成，作百王之模範，而三代以下，若漢之文帝，其亦可謂庶幾乎此焉者矣。
欽惟皇帝陛下，撫盈成之運，當鼎盛之年，聰睿有臨，得之天縱。日月所照，悉歸版圖，所謂能致之資、必致之勢，蓋兼而有之矣。如臣等一介草茅，未諳治體，迂疎之論，豈足以仰裨德業之隆？而明命下臨，天章煥爛，詢及乎庶富教之事，真誠懇惻，曾無一毫自大自滿之心。臣伏而讀之，有以見陛下克讓如唐堯，好生若虞舜，足以荷天眷之休，足以承祖業之重，足以為億兆之
translation_en:
Your servant, Mao Cheng.

Your servant replies: I have heard that whoever possesses all under Heaven must have the means to bring peace to all under Heaven and must consider how to lead it. The people of the realm are indeed those whom the ruler ought to bring peace, yet they cannot enjoy peace unless he personally sets an example for all under Heaven. Thus, only when nothing in his own conduct harms the people can he enrich them once they are numerous; and only when his own conduct offers the people a worthy model can he instruct them once they are prosperous. When they are both numerous and prosperous, the foundation on which they are established is secure, and all find their proper place. When they are both prosperous and instructed, their guidance is complete, and none transgresses what is right. This is how the emperors and kings of antiquity brought an entire age to prosperity and settled order and became models for successive sovereigns. Among those after the Three Dynasties, Emperor Wen of Han may also be said to have come close to this.

I reverently consider that Your Imperial Majesty presides over an age of abundant accomplishment and is in the prime of life. Your intelligence and discernment in ruling are Heaven’s generous endowment. All that the sun and moon illuminate falls within your registered domains. You thus possess both what are called the capacities to achieve these ends and the circumstances that make their achievement certain. Men such as your servant are mere commoners from the countryside, unversed in the essentials of government. How could our impractical and ill-informed discussions contribute to the grandeur of your virtue and achievements? Yet your illustrious command has descended to us, its imperial composition resplendent, asking about making the people numerous, enriching them, and instructing them. It is sincere, earnest, and deeply concerned, without the slightest trace of arrogance or complacency. Reading it in prostration, I perceive that Your Majesty is modest like Yao of Tang and cherishes life like Shun of Yu, worthy to receive the blessings of Heaven’s favor, worthy to sustain the weighty legacy of your ancestors, and worthy to be, for the countless millions, their …

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
君師而無慊也三復敬嘆之餘敢不竭其愚衷而對揚萬
一乎臣惟天生斯民立之司牧而寄以三事曰庶曰
富曰教而已庶而不富則無以厚民生富而不教則
無以正民德斯誠治道之不可闕者君人者於此有
失得而治效之隆替隨之故自昔守成之君夏有啓
商有高宗周有成康降是而下則僅有漢文帝誠如
聖策之所云者然較諸古之帝王則其德之醇疵治之大
小不能無所分辨而
聖心嘗慕之者所謂聞一善言見一善行沛然若決江河
而況善之在文帝其可取者尤非止於一端也觀其
===
===
席高祖新造之基啓西京近古之治家無不給人無
不足而殷富之效臻吏安其官民樂其業而醇厚之
風作兵革庶乎不試刑辟幾於弗用所以然者蓋不
惟其時為守令於郡縣者尚寬平而崇德化亦以其
修於身而後施諸天下凡治本之所存治具之所出
咸槩得之故其宮室苑囿車騎服御稍有不便輒弛
以利民欲作露臺召匠計直一聞百金之費則惜而
不為衣則弋綈也履則革舄也集囊為帷也編蒲為
席也所幸夫人衣不曳地也治霸陵皆瓦器不得以
金銀銅鐵為飾也欲厚風俗則止嗇夫之拜除誹謗
