如是，則可以涵養氣質，薫陶德性，進善之機難遏，肆情之事不形，心可得而正，身可得而脩矣。若夫敬畏之存，則當操持於不覩不聞之時，而省察於己所獨知之地；逸欲之戒，則當思夫伐性喪生之可懼，而念夫持盈守成之惟艱；言行之謹，則當使加乎民者靡尤，而見乎遠者無悔；威儀之正，則當肅肅於視朝之頃，雝雝於燕閒之時。夫如是，則內外交養，動靜不違，極中和樂之全，無偏倚駁雜之弊，心無不正，而身無不脩矣。
陛下心誠正，身誠脩，則天德純全，本源澄澈。由是所行者無非善政，不以其妨吾之欲而不行；所用者無非賢人，不以其拂吾之私而不用。政事以經之，賢才以紀之，將見九功惟叙，而禮義聿興；五典克從，而刑辟漸措。大治以致，大化以成。由是功光祖宗，由是業垂後裔，足以繼帝王之盛於隆古，足以陋文帝之小於下風。萬世而下，稱守成令主，豈能舍陛下而他適哉？蓋全天德以行王道者，本之所當先；致治化以紹隆古者，末之所宜後。伏惟陛下毋急其末而緩其本，毋重其所宜後而輕其所當先，深惟至計，永福蒼生，天下幸甚！臣不勝惓惓效忠之
translation_en:
…In this way, you can nurture your temperament and cultivate your moral character. The impulse to advance in goodness will be difficult to restrain, and acts of unbridled passion will not arise; your mind can thus be rectified and your person cultivated. As for maintaining reverence and awe, you should preserve them even when nothing is seen or heard, and examine yourself in matters known to yourself alone. To guard against ease and desire, you should consider the fearful prospect of damaging your nature and destroying your life, and remember how difficult it is to preserve prosperity and safeguard what has been achieved. To be circumspect in speech and conduct, you should ensure that what affects the people is without fault and that what becomes known afar gives no cause for regret. To make your bearing correct, you should be solemn when holding court and harmonious in your hours of leisure. In this way, inward and outward cultivation will sustain each other, and neither activity nor stillness will depart from what is proper. You will attain the fullness of equilibrium, harmony, and joy, without the faults of partiality or impurity. Your mind will be wholly rectified and your person fully cultivated.
If Your Majesty’s mind is truly rectified and your person truly cultivated, your Heaven-endowed virtue will be pure and complete, and its source clear. Consequently, everything you put into practice will be good government: you will not refrain from implementing it because it obstructs your desires. Everyone you employ will be worthy: you will not refuse to employ them because they oppose your private inclinations. With governmental affairs providing the warp and worthy men of talent providing the guiding threads, you will see the nine achievements duly ordered and ritual and righteousness flourishing; the five constant duties will be observed, and penal punishments will gradually be set aside. Great order will be attained, and great moral transformation accomplished. Through this, your achievements will bring glory to your ancestors, and your legacy will pass down to your descendants. You will be able to continue the flourishing rule of the emperors and kings of high antiquity and make Emperor Wen’s lesser accomplishments appear paltry by comparison. For ten thousand generations to come, when people speak of an excellent ruler who preserved his inheritance, how could they pass over Your Majesty and turn to anyone else? Preserving Heaven-endowed virtue in its entirety so as to practice the Kingly Way is the foundation and must come first; bringing about good government and moral transformation so as to carry on the achievements of high antiquity is the outcome and should follow. I humbly beseech Your Majesty not to hasten after the outcome while neglecting the foundation, nor to value what should follow while slighting what must come first. Reflect deeply upon this supreme plan and bring lasting blessings to the people: all under Heaven would be most fortunate! Your servant cannot contain his earnest devotion to serving loyally…

title: 弘治六年進士登科錄
text:
誠亦知愚陋無所裨益然芻蕘之言聖人擇焉伏惟
萬幾之暇少垂
睿覽苟有可采俯
賜施行臣不勝大願不勝大幸干冒
天威伏增惶悚臣謹對

translation_en: …sincerity. I also know that I am ignorant and uncultivated and have nothing beneficial to offer. Yet the sage selects what is useful even from the words of grass cutters and wood gatherers. I humbly beseech Your Majesty, in a moment of leisure amid the myriad affairs of state, to grant these words a little of your discerning attention. If anything merits adoption, condescend to put it into practice. Your servant could wish for nothing more and would count it the greatest good fortune. Having presumed to offend your imperial majesty, I bow in ever greater fear and trembling. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.
